programme_name: Immunoglobulin translocation and ER-quality control
functional_description: This programme coordinates the synthesis and ER translocation of immunoglobulin heavy and light chains with quality control mechanisms that prevent aggregation of misfolded proteins. The feature integrates signal peptide recognition (SEC11C), translocon-mediated co-translational translocation (SSR4), prolyl isomerase-catalyzed proper folding (FKBP11, FKBP2), and ER-associated protein degradation (HERPUD1, DERL3) to ensure only correctly folded antibodies are secreted.

programme_name: Endoplasmic reticulum protein synthesis and quality control
functional_description: This programme coordinates the specialized secretory pathway required for high-volume immunoglobulin production in plasma cells. It integrates ER translocon function (SSR4, SEC11C), molecular chaperone-mediated protein folding (HSP90B1), oxidative stress management (PRDX4), and proteasomal quality control (RAD23A, RBX1) to ensure proper antibody assembly and secretion while managing the proteotoxic stress of mass immunoglobulin synthesis.

programme_name: ER protein translocation and immunoglobulin folding
functional_description: This programme coordinates the translocation and post-translational processing of immunoglobulin proteins across the endoplasmic reticulum membrane. It couples signal sequence recognition (SSR4, SEC11C) with peptidyl-prolyl isomerase activity (FKBP11, FKBP2) required for proper folding of antibody heavy and light chains (IGHA1, IGHA2, IGLC2, IGLC3), and includes ER quality control mechanisms (HERPUD1, DERL3) to manage misfolded protein degradation.

programme_name: Plasma cell immunoglobulin secretion programme
Immunoglobulin assembly and ER protein folding
functional_description: This programme coordinates the synthesis and secretory pathway processing of immunoglobulin heavy and light chains (IGHG1/3/4, IGLC7, IGKC) in antibody-secreting plasma cells. programme_name: Plasma cell immunoglobulin secretion programme
Immunoglobulin assembly and ER-secretory pathway
functional_description: This programme coordinates the synthesis, folding, and secretion of immunoglobulin molecules in mature plasma cells. It integrates heavy chain (IGHM) and light chain (IGKC, IGKV variants) variable and constant region expression with the endoplasmic reticulum quality control machinery (HERPUD1, FKBP11, CRELD2) and protein translocation apparatus (SEC11C, SSR4). JCHAIN incorporation enables multimeric IgM assembly and mucosal homing.

programme_name: Immunoglobulin secretory pathway assembly
functional_description: This programme coordinates the synthesis and cotranslational translocation of immunoglobulin heavy and light chains into the endoplasmic reticulum for secretion. It encompasses both the variable (IGLV3-9, IGLV3-21, IGLV1-41) and constant (IGLC2, IGLC3, IGLC7, IGHG1, IGHG3, IGHG4) domain transcription, coupled with activation of the translocon machinery (SSR4, SEC11C) and peptidyl-prolyl isomerase activity (FKBP11) required for proper antibody folding. The enrichment of SDC1 and MZB1 further indicates a mature plasma cell secretory phenotype optimised for high-volume immunoglobulin export.
key_evidence: IGLC2/3/7, IGHG1/3/4: Complete Ig heavy and light chain constant regions enabling functional antibody assembly
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein complex delta subunit for cotranslational protein translocation across ER membrane
SEC11C: Signal peptidase complex component for cleavage of N-terminal signal sequences during translocation
FKBP11: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase catalysing proline-containing peptide bond isomerisation during Ig folding
SDC1: Plasma cell differentiation and maturation marker associated with antibody secretion capacity

programme_name: ER protein quality control in Ig secretion
functional_description: This programme coordinates endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein folding and quality control mechanisms specifically tuned to handle the high flux of immunoglobulin heavy and light chains (IGHG1/2, IGLC3) through the secretory pathway. The co-expression of translocon components (SSR4, SEC11C), ER chaperones (FKBP11), and ER-associated protein degradation machinery (HERPUD1, DERL3) with the XBP1 transcription factor indicates active unfolded protein response (UPR) signalling to maintain ER proteostasis during massive antibody synthesis.

FKBP11: peptidyl-prolyl isomerase catalysing proper folding of proline-rich Ig constant domains
HERPUD1, DERL3: ER-associated degradation (ERAD) pathway for disposal of misfolded Ig molecules

IGLC3, IGHG1/2: abundant substrate proteins requiring continuous ER processing capacity

programme_name: Immunoglobulin synthesis and ER quality control
functional_description: This programme coordinates immunoglobulin production with ER proteostasis mechanisms in plasma cells. It combines Ig lambda chain variable genes (IGLV3-27, IGLL5) with JCHAIN for multimeric antibody assembly, while simultaneously activating ER-resident chaperones (MANF, FKBP2) and ERAD machinery (DERL3) to manage the high protein synthesis load characteristic of antibody-secreting cells.

MANF, FKBP2: ER-resident chaperones maintaining proteostasis under secretory stress
SEC11C: signal peptidase complex subunit for Ig signal sequence processing and translocation
MZB1: B/plasma cell-specific regulator of proliferation and secretory capacity

programme_name: ER protein translocation and unfolded protein response
functional_description: This programme coordinates endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein processing machinery required for high-volume immunoglobulin secretion in plasma cells. It combines ER translocon components (SSR4, SEC11C) with ER-resident chaperones and quality control factors (HERPUD1, FKBP11, DERL3) that facilitate proper folding of secretory proteins and manage ER stress. XBP1 acts as the master transcriptional regulator of this response, activating genes essential for sustaining the biosynthetic capacity needed for antibody production.
key_evidence: SSR4: Translocon-associated protein complex subunit enabling signal sequence-dependent protein translocation across ER membrane
HERPUD1: ER stress sensor and ERAD component that triggers unfolded protein response when secretory load exceeds folding capacity

FKBP11: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase catalyzing proline-rich immunoglobulin domain folding
DERL3: ERAD component mediating retrotranslocation of misfolded proteins for proteasomal clearance

programme_name: ER protein translocation and UPR activation
functional_description: This programme coordinates endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein import machinery with unfolded protein response (UPR) signalling in antibody-secreting plasma cells. The translocon complex (SSR4, SEC11C) mediates co-translational translocation of immunoglobulin heavy and light chains (IGHA1, IGLC2, IGKC), while FKBP11 facilitates proline-rich domain folding and XBP1 drives UPR transcriptional responses. ER-resident quality control factors (DERL3, HERPUD1, PRDX4) manage proteostasis during high-volume antibody synthesis.
key_evidence: SSR4: delta subunit of translocon complex essential for Ig protein translocation across ER membrane
SEC11C: signal peptidase removes signal sequences from newly synthesized Ig chains during translocation
FKBP11: peptidyl-prolyl isomerase catalyses correct folding of Ig constant domains containing abundant prolines
XBP1: master UPR transcription factor activated by ER stress to upregulate chaperones and secretory capacity
DERL3 + HERPUD1: ER-associated degradation (ERAD) components removing terminally misfolded Ig molecules
IGHA1, IGLC2, IGKC: products of this translocation programme, confirming plasma cell identity
suggested_validation: Measure temporal correlation between XBP1s splicing (UPR activation marker) and translocon activity using surface plasmon resonance or co-immunoprecipitation of SSR4/SEC11C with nascent Ig chains in pulse-chase experiments on primary or differentiated plasma cells.

programme_name: ER proteostasis and immunoglobulin secretion
functional_description: This programme coordinates endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein folding, quality control, and trafficking machinery required for high-capacity immunoglobulin secretion in plasma cells. It combines ER chaperone function (HSP90B1, FKBP11, FKBP2), protein translocation (SSR4, SEC11C), disulfide bond formation (CRELD2, PRDX4), ERAD-mediated quality control (HERPUD1, DERL3), and ER stress adaptation (XBP1) to support the enormous biosynthetic demand of antibody production.
key_evidence: IGLC2 & IGHA1: cargo proteins defining the secretory output requiring ER processing
SSR4 & SEC11C: translocon and signal peptidase machinery for co-translational translocation
FKBP11 & FKBP2: peptidyl-prolyl isomerases catalyzing proline-containing antibody folding
CRELD2 & PRDX4: disulfide bond formation and redox homeostasis in oxidative ER lumen
HERPUD1 & DERL3: ERAD pathway for removing misfolded immunoglobulin intermediates
XBP1: master regulator of ER expansion and UPR-responsive gene expression in plasma cells

programme_name: Immunoglobulin maturation and ER protein quality control
functional_description: This programme coordinates the biosynthesis and post-translational maturation of immunoglobulin molecules in plasma cells through integrated endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein processing and quality control. It couples signal peptide cleavage (SEC11C), prolyl isomerization for proper Ig folding (FKBP11, FKBP2, PDIA4), disulfide bond formation (PDIA4, CRELD2), and ER-associated degradation of misfolded proteins (DERL3) to ensure assembly of functional antibodies for secretion.
key_evidence: SEC11C: signal peptidase required for N-terminal processing of nascent immunoglobulin heavy and light chains
FKBP11, FKBP2: prolyl isomerases essential for overcoming proline-induced folding barriers in immunoglobulin constant domains
PDIA4, CRELD2: protein disulfide isomerases catalysing inter- and intra-chain disulfide bond formation critical for Ig quaternary structure
DERL3: ERAD machinery component removing terminally misfolded Ig molecules to prevent aggregation
IGLC2, IGHA1, JCHAIN: structural Ig components whose translation is enabled by this ER proteostasis infrastructure
SSR4: translocon component maintaining ER translocation fidelity during high-volume Ig synthesis
suggested_validation: Quantitative proteomics comparing newly synthesized Ig heavy/light chain ratios and disulfide-linked Ig dimer abundance in plasma cells with genetic or chemical disruption of PDIA4 or DERL3, combined with ER stress markers (GRP78, XBP1s) to demonstrate the integrated quality control response.

programme_name: ER stress response in antibody-secreting plasma cells
functional_description: This programme captures the coordinated upregulation of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) unfolded protein response (UPR) machinery in plasma cells undergoing intense immunoglobulin synthesis. The dominance of plasma cells (87%) co-expressing immunoglobulin heavy and light chains (IGHG2, IGKC) alongside ER chaperones (HERPUD1, FKBP11), protein translocation machinery (SSR4, SEC11C), and the key UPR transcription factor XBP1 indicates active handling of the ER stress imposed by secretory antibody burden. Inclusion of SDC1 (syndecan-1/CD138, the canonical plasma cell marker) confirms these are differentiated antibody factories managing proteostatic stress.
key_evidence: IGHG2 & IGKC: Heavy and light chain immunoglobulins generating ER cargo load
HERPUD1: ER-resident ERAD component responding to unfolded protein accumulation
XBP1: Master UPR transcription factor for spliced isoform driving ER expansion
SSR4 & SEC11C: Translocon-associated complex for co-translational protein translocation
FKBP11: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase facilitating protein folding in ER
SDC1: Plasma cell differentiation marker confirming cell identity
suggested_validation: Perform ATAC-seq or ChIP-seq for XBP1 binding sites in sorted CD138+ plasma cells from this cluster, combined with RNA-seq after XBP1 inhibition (KIRA6 or genetic knockdown) to confirm UPR transcriptional dependence of this gene module.

programme_name: ER protein folding and immunoglobulin processing
functional_description: This programme coordinates endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein quality control mechanisms specifically required for high-volume immunoglobulin secretion in plasma cells. It encompasses signal peptide processing (SEC11C), prolyl isomerase-mediated protein folding (FKBP11), ER-resident chaperones (HSP90B1), and ERAD machinery (HERPUD1, DERL3, UBE2J1) to manage the proteostatic burden of antibody production.

XBP1: master transcription factor for UPR and ER expansion in plasma cells

suggested_validation: Perform surface plasmon resonance (SPR) or ELISA quantification of secreted Ig levels in plasma cells after CRISPR knockdown of FKBP11 or HSP90B1, compared to control, to confirm the essential role of this folding programme in Ig output.

programme_name: ER protein synthesis and unfolded protein response
functional_description: This programme coordinates endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein translocation, folding quality control, and unfolded protein response (UPR) activation in antibody-secreting plasma cells. The feature integrates translocon-mediated translocation machinery (SSR4, SEC11C), prolyl isomerase chaperones (FKBP11), ER stress sensors and ERAD components (HERPUD1, DERL3, XBP1), alongside the immunoglobulin constant regions (IGKC, IGHA1, IGHG3) that serve as the primary cargo being processed.

suggested_validation: Pharmacological UPR induction (e.g. tunicamycin treatment) or XBP1 splicing analysis combined with surface proteomics to confirm coordinated upregulation of translocon, chaperone, and ERAD components specifically in high-Ig-secreting plasma cells versus resting B cells

programme_name: Immunoglobulin lambda chain synthesis and ER translocation
functional_description: This programme coordinates production of immunoglobulin lambda light chains with active ER protein translocation machinery. The dominant lambda variable (IGLV) and constant (IGLL) gene expression, combined with signal sequence recognition (SSR4) and ER translocon components (SEC11C), indicates coordinated synthesis of lambda-containing antibodies destined for secretion. The presence of prolyl isomerases (FKBP11, FKBP2) supports proper antibody domain folding.

IGLV2-14, IGLV2-23, IGLV1-40, IGLV3-21: Clonal lambda variable domain expression—specific antibody specificity

FKBP11, FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases—domain folding catalyst for proper Ig tertiary structure

suggested_validation: Perform surface immunoglobulin staining stratified by light chain type (lambda vs kappa) combined with ER-tracker live imaging in sorted plasma cells to confirm lambda-specific ER localization and translational coupling in feature-high vs feature-low cells.

programme_name: ER protein folding and immunoglobulin secretion
functional_description: This programme coordinates the unfolded protein response (UPR) with immunoglobulin assembly and secretion in plasma cells. It combines ER translocon machinery (SSR4, SEC11C) with molecular chaperones (HSP90B1, FKBP11, FKBP2) and ERAD components (HERPUD1, DERL3, UBE2J1) to manage the massive protein folding load imposed by antibody production, while supporting IgA/IgM polymerization (JCHAIN) and redox homeostasis (PRDX4).

SSR4/SEC11C: Signal sequence recognition and peptidase processing during co-translational translocation
HSP90B1/FKBP11/FKBP2: Prolyl isomerase and chaperone activities essential for antibody domain folding
HERPUD1/DERL3/UBE2J1: ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD) pathway for misfolded antibodies

programme_name: Immunoglobulin synthesis with ER protein quality control
functional_description: This programme coordinates the high-flux production of immunoglobulins (IgA, IgG, IgK heavy and light chains) in plasma cells with active endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein quality control. The feature captures both the massive translational output of antibodies (requiring SSR4/SEC11C translocon machinery) and the ER stress response machinery (XBP1, HERPUD1, DERL3) needed to manage proteotoxic load from misfolded antibody intermediates.

HERPUD1/DERL3: ERAD ubiquitin ligase adaptors that target misfolded proteins for proteasomal degradation under ER stress
FKBP11: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase supporting proper folding of immunoglobulin domains containing multiple prolines
suggested_validation: Perform XBP1 splicing assay (qRT-PCR for spliced vs unspliced XBP1) combined with pulse-chase labeling of newly synthesized immunoglobulins to quantify the relationship between UPR activation intensity and antibody synthesis/secretion capacity in sorted plasma cells.

programme_name: ER protein synthesis and UPR in antibody secretion
functional_description: This programme coordinates endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein quality control with high-capacity antibody synthesis in plasma cells. It combines immunoglobulin heavy (IGHG1, IGHG3) and light chain (IGKC) production with ER translocon machinery (SSR4, SEC11C), protein folding chaperones (FKBP11), and unfolded protein response (UPR) components (XBP1, HERPUD1). This reflects the metabolic stress of secreting vast quantities of antibodies.

SSR4, SEC11C: ER translocon and signal peptidase complex for co-translational translocation of nascent immunoglobulins
XBP1: master UPR transcription factor that drives ER expansion and chaperone expression in response to antibody synthesis burden
HERPUD1, FKBP11: ER-resident protein folding and quality control factors handling misfolded antibody intermediates
SDC1: syndecan-1 is a canonical plasma cell maturation marker and ER stress sensor
suggested_validation: Perform XBP1 splicing qPCR and ATF4 phosphorylation immunofluorescence on high-expressing vs low-expressing plasma cells from feature 1581, combined with ER stress-induced apoptosis assays (tunicamycin treatment) to confirm UPR dependency.

programme_name: ER protein translocation and disulfide bond maturation
functional_description: This programme coordinates the endoplasmic reticulum-dependent secretory pathway required for high-volume immunoglobulin production in plasma cells. It encompasses signal peptide recognition and cleavage (SEC11C), co-translational translocation through the translocon (SSR4), and oxidative protein folding with disulfide isomerase activity (FKBP11, FKBP2, CRELD2), supported by ER-resident quality control factors (HERPUD1, DERL3, ERLEC1) that manage misfolded protein accumulation.

SEC11C: signal peptidase complex catalyses N-terminal signal sequence removal during translocation

HERPUD1/DERL3/ERLEC1: ER stress response and ERAD machinery to manage folding-stressed accumulated immunoglobulins
IGLC2/IGHD: immunoglobulin products being processed through this translocational machinery

programme_name: ER protein translocation and immunoglobulin secretion
functional_description: This programme coordinates endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein translocation machinery with immunoglobulin heavy and light chain synthesis and secretion in plasma cells. The feature integrates signal sequence recognition (SSR4, SEC11C), ER translocation, protein folding (FKBP11), and quality control (HERPUD1) with abundant immunoglobulin constant regions (IGHG1/3/4, IGKC, IGLC2), enabling high-throughput secretion of functional antibodies.
key_evidence: SSR4: core translocon component required for co-translational translocation of signal peptide-bearing immunoglobulins
SEC11C: signal peptidase essential for signal peptide cleavage during ER entry of secretory proteins
FKBP11: prolyl isomerase catalysing proper folding of proline-rich immunoglobulin domains
HERPUD1: ER-resident ubiquitin ligase mediating quality control of misfolded immunoglobulins
IGHG1/3/4, IGKC, IGLC2: abundant constant regions of secretory immunoglobulin chains requiring active translocation
suggested_validation: Use selective inhibition of SEC61A/translocon (e.g., selinexor or targeted photocrosslinking) combined with quantitative proteomics to show coordinated collapse of both ER translocation machinery and immunoglobulin heavy/light chain synthesis, plus measurement of extracellular antibody titre to confirm secretion defects.

programme_name: ER protein synthesis and unfolded protein response
functional_description: This programme coordinates the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) quality control and protein folding machinery required for high-volume immunoglobulin synthesis in plasma cells. It integrates signal sequence recognition (SSR4, SEC11C), prolyl isomerase-mediated protein folding (FKBP11), ER-associated degradation (DERL3, HERPUD1), and protective oxidative stress responses (SELENOM), enabling the massive secretory burden of antibody production while preventing ER stress-induced apoptosis.
key_evidence: SSR4: translocon-associated protein complex component for co-translational translocation of immunoglobulins
SEC11C: signal peptidase complex subunit required for N-terminal signal peptide cleavage during Ig synthesis
FKBP11: prolyl isomerase catalysing cis/trans peptide bond isomerisation, essential for Ig domain folding
DERL3: ER-resident derlin mediating ERAD of misfolded Ig chains to prevent aggregation
HERPUD1: UPR effector induced by ER stress to prevent accumulation of unfolded proteins

programme_name: Heme biosynthesis and globin chain synthesis
functional_description: This programme coordinates the early erythroid differentiation stage characterized by simultaneous heme biosynthesis initiation and globin gene expression. ALAS2 catalyzes the first committed step of heme synthesis in mitochondria, while HBA1, HBA2, HBB, and HBG1 encode the globin polypeptide chains required for functional hemoglobin assembly. CMPK2 supports nucleotide biosynthesis needed for the massive translational demand of globin protein production during basophilic and early polychromatic erythroblast stages.

HBA1/HBA2/HBB/HBG1: structural hemoglobin subunit genes requiring coordinated expression for functional tetrameric hemoglobin

DMTN: actin-binding protein establishing membrane skeleton required for RBC maturation post-hemoglobinization
suggested_validation: Quantify heme content and globin protein:heme ratio across FACS-sorted erythroblast stages; confirm ALAS2 and globin mRNA co-expression via dual RNA-FISH; measure heme synthesis flux using 14C-glycine incorporation in isolated mitochondria from feature-high vs feature-low cells

programme_name: Ribosomal biogenesis and mitochondrial chaperone support
functional_description: This programme coordinates ribosomal RNA processing and ribosomal protein assembly (NPM1, NCL, GAR1, PA2G4, RPL22L1) with mitochondrial protein quality control (HSPD1, HSPE1, HSP90AB1). This pairing reflects the bioenergetic demands of erythroid proliferation: ribosomal biogenesis requires massive ATP consumption, necessitating concurrent mitochondrial chaperone activity to maintain redox balance and prevent proteotoxic stress during rapid translation machinery expansion.

NCL/PA2G4/GAR1: pre-rRNA processing and snoRNP assembly components
HSPD1/HSPE1: mitochondrial ATP-dependent chaperonins supporting high-demand oxidative metabolism
HSP90AB1: molecular chaperone stabilizing signaling proteins during proliferative stress
RPL22L1: structural ribosomal protein confirming translation machinery synthesis
suggested_validation: Measure steady-state mitochondrial ATP production and protein carbonyl content in pro-erythroblasts with NPM1 knockdown vs control; increased oxidative stress and ATP depletion would confirm the energetic coupling between ribosomal biogenesis and mitochondrial chaperone demand.

programme_name: Erythroid membrane protein biosynthesis
functional_description: A coordinated programme for biosynthesis and trafficking of blood group antigens and ion transporters essential for mature erythrocyte function. This involves expression of Rh (RHCE, RHD) and Diego (SLC4A1) blood group systems, ganglioside remodelling via sialylation (ST8SIA1), and metabolic support through carbonic anhydrase (CA1) for CO2 transport. The programme is activated during the transition from pro-erythroblast through polychromatic stages when functional RBC protein assembly becomes critical.
key_evidence: RHCE/RHD: Rh blood group antigen expression—clinically critical erythroid surface determinants synthesised de novo during early differentiation
SLC4A1: AE1 anion exchanger—essential for CO2/HCO3− transport and erythrocyte osmotic stability; Diego blood group antigen

BCAM: Lutheran glycoprotein—immunoglobulin superfamily adhesion molecule and blood group antigen

programme_name: Lymphocyte activation and immune response

IGHV1-2: Immunoglobulin heavy chain variable region; direct evidence of B-cell origin

The co-expression pattern reflects the metabolic coupling required in pro- and basophilic erythroblasts, where heme availability must match globin translation demand to prevent toxic free globin accumulation.

NCOA4: selective autophagy receptor for ferritin degradation, releasing iron for heme synthesis in mitochondria during early erythroid expansion

programme_name: Myeloid contamination in erythroid sorting
functional_description: This feature represents co-enriched myeloid genes rather than a true erythroid metabolic programme. programme_name: Mitochondrial OXPHOS and ribosome biogenesis
functional_description: This programme coordinates oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) capacity with ribosomal assembly and translation machinery in early erythroid progenitors. The co-activation of mitochondrial electron transport chain components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1) with ribosomal proteins and translation factors reflects the high biosynthetic demand during pro-erythroblast expansion, when cells require both ATP generation and rapid protein synthesis to support haemoglobin production.

functional_description: This feature appears to represent technical noise rather than a genuine biological programme. MTRNR2L1 and CRNDE: Pseudogenes and lncRNAs without established erythroid biology
KIAA0226L, CCDC191, LL22NC03-2H8.5: Uncharacterized genes with no functional annotation

programme_name: Erythroid lineage contamination and pseudogene artifacts
functional_description: This feature predominantly reflects technical artifacts and non-functional sequences rather than a coherent biological programme. programme_name: T cell activation and immune synapse assembly
functional_description: This feature represents T cell activation programming, not erythroid metabolism as previously annotated. Key genes include TOX2 (T cell lineage commitment transcription factor), BACH2 (adaptive immune response regulator), WASF1 (actin polymerization in immune synapse), and CD79B (B cell receptor signaling), indicating active T cell receptor signaling and cytoskeletal reorganization during immune activation.

programme_name: Plasma cell immunoglobulin secretory apparatus
functional_description: This feature represents the secretory pathway machinery and immunoglobulin production programme active in antibody-secreting plasma cells, not early erythroid bioenergetics as previously annotated. The dominant genes encode immunoglobulin heavy chains (IGHG1, IGHG3), light chains (IGKC, IGKV1D-17), and plasma cell markers (SDC1/CD138, FCRL5). Co-expression of ER protein retention receptors (KDELR3) and signal peptidase machinery (SEC11C) reflects the massive secretory burden of plasma cells producing antibodies.

SDC1: Canonical plasma cell marker and syndecan-1, a heparan sulfate proteoglycan critical for plasma cell localization and survival
KDELR3, SEC11C: ER-resident protein retention and signal peptide processing machinery essential for high-volume protein secretion

TNFRSF17: BCMA, a plasma cell survival factor with no erythroid function

programme_name: Plasma cell contamination in erythroid sorting

IGHG3: Immunoglobulin heavy constant gamma; B cell-specific, not erythroid

MZB1: Marginal zone B cell marker; directly indicates B cell lineage contamination

MZB1: Marginal zone B cell specific protein, plasma cell lineage marker

programme_name: Immunoglobulin contamination in erythroid sorting

PTRF: caveolin-associated protein involved in membrane organisation and endocytic trafficking
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence imaging of KRT79, phalloidin F-actin staining, and EXOC3L2 localisation in sorted pro-erythroblast and basophilic erythroblast populations to visualise cytoskeletal dynamics and membrane trafficking activity during the early erythroid transition.

programme_name: Cytoskeletal remodeling and membrane dynamics early erythropoiesis
functional_description: This programme is active in pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts and reflects early-stage remodeling of cellular architecture rather than bioenergetics per se. The enrichment of cytoskeletal proteins (TUBB1), membrane transporters (AQP10), and adaptor proteins (DAB2) suggests active reorganization of the plasma membrane and intracellular transport systems accompanying rapid cell division and volume changes during early erythroid commitment. The presence of histone genes (HIST1H2AC) alongside these factors indicates concurrent active chromatin remodeling.
key_evidence: TUBB1: beta-tubulin essential for spindle assembly and cytoskeletal dynamics during rapid mitotic divisions in early erythroblasts
AQP10: aquaglyceroporin mediating water/glycerol transport critical for osmotic regulation and cell volume changes during erythroid differentiation
DAB2: mitogen-responsive adaptor protein regulating endocytic trafficking and membrane protein internalization in proliferating cells
HIST1H2AC: active histone variant expression required for chromatin accessibility during erythroid lineage specification
suggested_validation: Perform live-cell imaging of pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts tracking TUBB1-GFP dynamics and aquaporin-mediated water transport using fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) to directly measure membrane remodeling kinetics during early erythropoiesis.

programme_name: Aberrant immunoglobulin expression in erythroid progenitors
functional_description: This feature captures ectopic immunoglobulin gene expression (heavy and light chain variable and constant regions: IGHM, IGHV2-5, IGHV4-55, IGLV1-44, IGLV4-60, IGLL5, JCHAIN) predominantly in basophilic and pro-erythroblasts. This represents either (1) transdifferentiation or cellular confusion at the erythroid-B cell developmental crossroads, or (2) aberrant transcriptional reactivation of silenced B cell loci in early erythroid cells. The presence of SEC11C and signal peptidase machinery suggests these immunoglobulin transcripts may reach translation stages.
key_evidence: IGHM: immunoglobulin mu heavy constant chain—core B cell product, ectopically expressed in 46.5% basophilic erythroblasts
JCHAIN: joining chain for multimeric immunoglobulins—terminal step of Ig assembly, incompatible with erythroid differentiation
SEC11C: signal peptidase for ER translocation—indicates immunoglobulin secretory pathway activation in cells committed to enucleation
EPB41L4B: erythrocyte membrane protein—genuine erythroid marker mixed with immunoglobulin programme, suggesting feature captures transitional/confused state
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry or immunofluorescence to quantify surface immunoglobulin protein on sorted basophilic erythroblasts (CD71+GPA+) vs B cells; single-cell RNA-seq with TCR/BCR enrichment to confirm these are bona fide erythroid cells mis-expressing B cell genes, not B cell contamination.

programme_name: Plasma cell contamination with erythroid signal
functional_description: This feature primarily captures immunoglobulin genes (IGLC7, IGLV1-51, IGLV6-57, IGHG1) and plasma cell markers (CD38), indicating contamination from the 1% plasma cell population rather than a true erythroid programme. The presence of TP53INP1 (autophagy), PERP (apoptosis), and CAV1 (membrane trafficking) suggests stress response and protein secretion machinery characteristic of antibody-secreting cells, not erythroid mitochondrial bioenergetics.
key_evidence: IGLC7, IGLV1-51, IGLV6-57: Immunoglobulin light chain genes absent in erythroid lineage
IGHG1: Immunoglobulin heavy chain characteristic of plasma cells, not erythroid cells
CD38: Plasma cell marker with NAD+ hydrolase function for cell communication
TP53INP1: Autophagy/UPR marker reflecting protein secretion stress in plasma cells
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein involved in antibody translocation across ER
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting of CD38+/CD19+ plasma cells vs. CD71+/CD235a+ early erythroblasts followed by qPCR validation of IGLC7, IGLV6-57, and IGHG1 expression to confirm these genes segregate exclusively with plasma cells, not erythroid populations.
prior_programme_name: Early erythroid mitochondrial bioenergetics and proliferation

programme_name: Plasma cell contamination artifact
functional_description: This feature reflects technical contamination of the early erythroid cluster with plasma cell transcripts rather than a genuine erythroid programme. The top genes are dominated by immunoglobulin heavy and light chain genes (IGHA1, IGLC7, IGLV3-21, IGHV3-23) characteristic of antibody-secreting cells, despite nominal 1% plasma cell composition. The presence of SEC11C, SSR4, and DERL3 (ER/translocon machinery) and DPEP1 reflect the massive protein synthesis and secretory load of plasma cells, not erythroid bioenergetics.
key_evidence: IGHA1, IGLC7, IGLV3-21, IGHV3-23: immunoglobulin genes incompatible with erythroid lineage
SEC11C, SSR4, DERL3: endoplasmic reticulum translocation complex, hallmark of plasma cell secretory machinery
CCR10: chemokine receptor associated with plasma cell homing and immune response, not erythroid function
CDKN2A: cell cycle arrest regulator, elevated in non-dividing plasma cells rather than proliferating early erythroblasts
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sort of early erythroblasts (CD71+, CD235a+, CD34−) followed by qPCR validation that IGHA1, IGLC7, and immunoglobulin genes are absent or dramatically reduced in pure erythroid populations, confirming they represent doublet/multiplet contamination rather than genuine FP.

programme_name: Megakaryocyte contamination in early erythroblasts
functional_description: This feature does not represent an erythroid-specific programme but rather reflects transcriptional contamination from megakaryocytic lineage genes. The top genes are predominantly megakaryocyte markers (PPBP, PF4V1, GP6, ITGB3, F13A1) involved in platelet biogenesis, adhesion, and coagulation, with structural proteins (MYL9, CALD1) characteristic of megakaryocyte cytoplasmic organization rather than erythroid mitochondrial function.
key_evidence: PPBP: platelet-derived growth factor and CXC chemokine, canonical megakaryocyte secretory protein
GP6: platelet collagen receptor, not expressed in erythroid lineage
ITGB3: integrin beta-3 subunit essential for platelet adhesion and aggregation
PF4V1: platelet factor 4 variant, exclusively megakaryocyte-derived chemokine
F13A1: coagulation factor XIII, megakaryocyte product for hemostasis
MYL9: myosin light chain involved in megakaryocyte contractile apparatus organization
suggested_validation: Perform flow cytometry sorting of pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts with megakaryocyte-specific markers (CD61, CD42b) to quantify contamination; re-analyze SAE on rigorously gated, lineage-pure erythroid populations to identify true mitochondrial biogenesis programmes (which should include NRF1, TFAM, COX genes)

programme_name: ER protein quality control in early erythroid
functional_description: This feature captures endoplasmic reticulum (ER) proteostasis machinery activated in pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts. The programme centres on ER-resident chaperones (KDELR3), protein translocation machinery (SSR4, translocon components), ER-associated degradation (DERL3), and KDEL-mediated protein retention—essential for managing the massive flux of newly synthesized globin chains and other secretory/membrane proteins during early erythroid differentiation.
key_evidence: DERL3: ER-associated degradation component for removing misfolded proteins, critical when translational demand peaks
KDELR3: KDEL receptor that retrieves ER-resident chaperones, maintaining ER protein quality control capacity
SSR4: Core translocon-associated protein required for co-translational translocation of secretory proteins into ER lumen
CAV2: Caveolin involved in membrane trafficking and ER-to-Golgi transport coordination
suggested_validation: Perform co-immunofluorescence on sorted pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts using DERL3, KDELR3, and SSR4 antibodies to confirm co-localisation at ER and assess ER stress markers (CHOP, BiP) by qRT-PCR to validate active proteostasis signalling during this differentiation stage.

programme_name: Stress response and proteostasis in early erythroblasts
functional_description: This programme reflects activation of heat shock protein (HSP70) and TRIM-mediated protein quality control mechanisms in pro-erythroblasts and basophilic erythroblasts during early proliferative stages. The dominance of HSPA1B—a canonical stress-response chaperone—alongside TRIM40 (a negative regulator of protein stability) suggests coordinated management of proteostatic stress during the metabolically intense early erythroid differentiation phase, when rapid haemoglobin synthesis and organellar transitions create proteotoxic burden.
key_evidence: HSPA1B: ATP-dependent molecular chaperone essential for protein folding and aggregation prevention under metabolic stress
TRIM40: TRIM family E3 ubiquitin ligase providing proteasomal degradation pathway for misfolded proteins
TUBB1: β-tubulin isoform supporting cytoskeletal remodelling during erythroblast shape changes and mitochondrial positioning
suggested_validation: Measure HSP70 protein levels and chaperone activity (ATP-dependent refolding assays) in FACS-sorted pro-erythroblasts vs basophilic erythroblasts, alongside proteasome activity assays to confirm proteostatic demand in early erythroid differentiation
prior_programme_name: Early erythroblast mitochondrial biogenesis and proliferation

programme_name: Plasma cell contamination in erythroid preparation
functional_description: This feature represents immunoglobulin and plasma cell-specific gene expression, not erythroid mitochondrial bioenergetics. The top genes are predominantly immunoglobulin light chain (IGLC, IGLV) and heavy chain (IGHG) genes, along with plasma cell markers (MZB1) and ER/secretory pathway components (SSR4, SEC11C) required for antibody synthesis. The 3.5% plasma cell contamination in the cell composition explains this transcriptional programme.
key_evidence: IGLC7, IGLV genes: immunoglobulin variable and constant regions essential for antibody assembly
MZB1: marginal zone B/plasma cell marker involved in B cell proliferation and antibody production
SSR4, SEC11C: translocon and signal peptidase components required for ER translocation and antibody secretion
CCR10: B cell homing receptor directing plasma cells to mucosal tissues
suggested_validation: Perform fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) to separate CD19+CD38+ plasma cells from CD34+CD71+ erythroid progenitors, then re-analyse SAE features independently to confirm this represents batch contamination rather than genuine erythroid biology.

programme_name: Plasma cell contamination artifact
functional_description: This feature does not represent early erythroid bioenergetics but rather captures plasma cell-associated genes, likely due to technical contamination or ambient RNA in the dataset. The presence of JCHAIN, IGHA2 (immunoglobulin genes), TNFRSF17 (BCMA), and CCR10 (plasma cell homing receptor) are diagnostic plasma cell markers that are mechanistically incompatible with erythroid differentiation. The enrichment in basophilic erythroblasts (46%) appears insufficient to explain the strong plasma cell gene signal.
key_evidence: JCHAIN: joining chain for multimeric immunoglobulins—exclusive to plasma cells/B cells
IGHA2: immunoglobulin heavy chain constant region—plasma cell antibody production
TNFRSF17: BCMA receptor for plasma cell survival signals (APRIL/BAFF pathway)
CCR10: chemokine receptor for plasma cell homing to bone marrow niches
TXNDC5: ER protein disulfide isomerase for antibody folding—plasma cell ER expansion
suggested_validation: Perform fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) or single-molecule RNA detection on feature-positive cells to distinguish whether these genes are genuinely co-expressed in single erythroblasts or represent doublets/ambient RNA from nearby plasma cells. Sort basophilic erythroblasts by strict morphology and confirm absence of JCHAIN/IGHA2 by qRT-PCR.

programme_name: Immunoglobulin contamination in erythroid preparation
functional_description: This feature represents aberrant immunoglobulin gene expression (heavy and light chain variable and constant regions) detected in early erythroid cells, likely reflecting contamination from plasma cells or B cells rather than a genuine erythroid differentiation programme. The presence of IGHV3-21, IGLV variants, and IGLC3 indicates clonal or oligoclonal B cell contamination (~2% plasma cells in the activating population), despite the dominant erythroid signature.
key_evidence: IGHV3-21: Immunoglobulin heavy chain variable region—hallmark of B cell/plasma cell identity, incompatible with erythroid differentiation
IGLC3: Immunoglobulin lambda constant chain (Kern-Oz marker)—indicates mature or maturing plasma cells, not erythroid cells
IGLV2-11, IGLV3-21, IGLV4-3: Multiple immunoglobulin lambda light chain variable regions—consistent with clonal B cell expansion, not erythroid transcription
suggested_validation: Flow cytometric gating on CD19+/CD38+ plasma cells vs. CD71+/CD235a+ erythroid cells to confirm the 2% plasma cell contamination; single-cell RNA-seq verification to demonstrate that immunoglobulin genes are expressed exclusively in the plasma cell subpopulation, not in erythroid cells themselves.
prior_programme_name: Early erythroid differentiation and mitochondrial biogenesis

programme_name: Plasma cell contamination artifact
functional_description: This feature does not represent an erythroid differentiation programme despite the cluster composition. The top genes are dominated by immunoglobulin heavy chains (IGHG1, IGHG3, IGHG4) and immunoglobulin light chains (IGLV6-57), along with plasma cell markers (TNFRSF13B/TACI). These genes are incompatible with erythroid biology and indicate contaminating plasma cell transcripts in the erythroid cluster.
key_evidence: IGHG1/IGHG3/IGHG4: Immunoglobulin constant regions only expressed in plasma cells, not erythroid cells
IGLV6-57: Immunoglobulin light chain variable region—plasma cell-specific immune protein
TNFRSF13B: TACI is a lymphocyte-specific TNF receptor absent from erythroid differentiation
CHAC1: Gamma-glutamylcyclotransferase involved in oxidative stress response during antibody secretion, not erythroid differentiation
suggested_validation: FACS sort basophilic erythroblasts by CD71+/CD11b- gating (excluding CD45+ contamination) and re-analyse SAE feature activation in pure erythroid cells to confirm this is a sorting/batch artifact rather than a true erythroid programme.

programme_name: Plasma cell immunoglobulin secretion and ER proteostasis
functional_description: This feature represents the endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response (ER-UPR) and protein secretion machinery active in antibody-secreting plasma cells. The programme coordinates immunoglobulin heavy and light chain assembly (IGHM, IGLC3, JCHAIN) with ER chaperones (HSP90B1, PDIA4, SDF2L1) and ER proteostasis factors (CRELD2, FKBP11, SEC11C) required for high-volume antibody synthesis and secretion. The ER stress sensor MANF indicates active ER quality control during the massive protein synthesis burden characteristic of plasma cells.
key_evidence: IGHM, IGLC3, JCHAIN: immunoglobulin structural components requiring coordinated assembly in ER lumen
PDIA4, CRELD2, SDF2L1, FKBP11: protein disulfide isomerases and ER chaperones essential for Ig folding and oligomerization
HSP90B1: ATP-dependent chaperone stabilizing partially folded Ig domains during secretory pathway transit
MANF: ER-localized neurotrophic factor and ER stress modulator indicating UPR activation
SEC11C: signal peptidase for co-translational processing of secreted Ig molecules
TNFRSF17: BCMA, plasma cell survival receptor enriched in mature antibody-secreting cells
suggested_validation: Sort cells from the top 200 activating set by CD138+/CD19- plasma cell markers and compare ER stress markers (BiP, phospho-IRE1α, XBP1s splicing) and immunoglobulin secretion rate (ELISA of culture supernatant) between high-feature and low-feature populations.

programme_name: Aberrant immunoglobulin expression in erythroid precursors
functional_description: This feature represents ectopic expression of immunoglobulin genes (IGKV, IGLV, IGHD, IGHV) and B-cell-associated transcripts in early erythroid cells, particularly basophilic and pro-erythroblasts. The dominant presence of immunoglobulin variable and constant regions suggests either contamination from co-sorted plasma cells (~1% in cluster), cross-lineage transcription noise, or potentially aberrant transcriptional activation in the erythroid compartment. Supporting genes like SSR4 (translocon component) and selenoproteins indicate possible protein synthesis machinery activation, though the biological relevance to erythroid differentiation is questionable.
key_evidence: IGKV2-29, IGKV2D-29, IGLV2-18: immunoglobulin variable domains—hallmark B-cell/plasma cell transcripts with no known erythroid function
IGHD, IGHV3-30: immunoglobulin heavy chain segments—highly specific to B-lineage, inconsistent with ~90% erythroid cell composition
SSR4: translocon-associated protein complex, supports active secretory pathway protein synthesis incompatible with mature erythroid biology
IGLL5: immunoglobulin lambda-like polypeptide in immunoglobulin locus—reinforces B-cell lineage signature
suggested_validation: Sort basophilic erythroblasts by CD34+CD71+ markers and verify immunoglobulin transcripts via RT-qPCR and in situ hybridization to confirm whether these represent genuine erythroid transcription, plasma cell contamination, or SAE noise artifact; alternatively, use single-cell multiomics (protein+RNA) to disambiguate cell identity.

programme_name: Plasma cell contamination in erythroid sorting
functional_description: This feature primarily represents plasma cell immunoglobulin production (IGHG3, IGHV3-64, IGLVI-70) and associated secretory pathway machinery (SSR4, FKBP11), with minimal genuine erythroid programme content. The 85% erythroid cell composition likely reflects sorting contamination or transient co-expression during early B-to-plasma cell differentiation, rather than an authentic erythroid mitochondrial biogenesis programme. XBP1 and SDC1 further support plasma cell identity rather than erythroid progenitor biology.
key_evidence: IGHG3, IGHV3-64, IGLVI-70: immunoglobulin heavy/light chain constant and variable regions—diagnostic of antibody-secreting cells, not erythroid progenitors
SSR4, FKBP11: translocon and ER protein folding machinery—critical for immunoglobulin secretion, inconsistent with mitochondrial biogenesis
XBP1: master regulator of unfolded protein response in plasma cells, not an erythroid differentiation factor
SDC1: plasma cell surface marker and heparan sulfate proteoglycan involved in B cell biology
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting by CD138/SDC1 and CD19 to separate genuine plasma cells from erythroid population, then re-train SAE on purified cell types to confirm whether this feature disappears or reassigns to plasma cell clusters

programme_name: Plasma cell contamination with ER-stress markers
functional_description: This feature captures a minor but distinct contamination signature of plasma cell immunoglobulin genes (IGLC7, IGLV3-21, IGHA1, IGHV3-23) co-expressed with endoplasmic reticulum stress response and protein processing machinery (SEC11C, SSR4, DERL3). The ER-associated degradation (ERAD) components and signal peptidase activity indicate active antibody synthesis and secretory pathway flux, inconsistent with the stated early erythroid progenitor annotation.
key_evidence: IGLC7, IGHA1, IGLV3-21, IGHV3-23: Plasma cell-specific immunoglobulin constant and variable domains; >10% of top genes are antibody components
SEC11C, SSR4: Signal peptidase complex subunits required for translocation of secretory proteins (antibodies) across ER membrane
DERL3: ERAD component indicating ER proteostasis burden from high-rate antibody synthesis and misfolded protein clearance
suggested_validation: Perform flow cytometric sorting of CD19+CD138+ plasma cells vs CD34+CD71+ erythroid progenitors and validate feature activation pattern; confirm <1% plasma cell contribution to the defining 200 cells does not drive the signature.

programme_name: Plasma cell immunoglobulin synthesis programme
functional_description: This feature captures the immunoglobulin heavy and light chain variable and constant region gene expression characteristic of differentiated plasma cells, combined with endoplasmic reticulum protein processing machinery required for antibody synthesis and secretion. The co-expression of IGLL5, IGLL1, immunoglobulin variable segments (IGLV, IGHV), constant regions (IGHG2), and ER-resident quality control proteins (ERLEC1, DERL3, SSR4) reflects the massive translational and secretory burden of antibody-producing cells.
key_evidence: IGLL5/IGLL1: Immunoglobulin lambda-like polypeptides essential for pre-B cell receptor and mature antibody assembly
IGLV2-14/IGHV4-55: Rearranged variable region segments encoding antibody antigen-binding domains
IGHG2: Heavy chain constant region enabling IgG isotype antibody function and Fc-mediated immunity
ERLEC1/DERL3/SSR4: ER translocon and lectin components required for co-translational protein translocation of immunoglobulins
SDC1/CD38: Plasma cell surface markers associated with antibody secretion and terminal differentiation
MZB1: Marginal zone B cell/plasma cell maturation factor
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting of CD38+SDC1+ plasma cells followed by qPCR/RNA-seq validation of immunoglobulin heavy/light chain mRNA and comparison of ER protein processing gene expression between this population and early erythroid cells to demonstrate lineage-specific activation.

programme_name: Myeloid contamination in erythroid progenitors
functional_description: This feature captures aberrant myeloid gene expression co-activating with early erythroid progenitors, likely representing either genuine myeloid contamination in the sorted population or cells at a bipotent progenitor stage. The presence of MNDA (myeloid lineage marker), LYZ (monocyte/neutrophil marker), CEBPD (myeloid transcription factor), and actin-regulatory proteins (CAPG) alongside erythroid enrichment suggests incomplete lineage commitment or technical batch effects rather than a bona fide erythroid mitochondrial biogenesis programme.
key_evidence: MNDA: Strictly detects granulocyte-monocyte lineage nuclei; absent in pure erythroid differentiation
LYZ: Monocyte/neutrophil antimicrobial enzyme; incompatible with erythroid function
CEBPD: Myeloid C/EBP family transcription factor driving monocytic differentiation
CAPG: Actin-capping protein enriched in myeloid cells for motility, not erythroid maturation
MS4A4A: Myeloid membrane protein family member, contraindicated in mature erythroid lineage
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sort purification of CD34+ pro-erythroblasts using CD71 (early erythroid marker) and CD33/CD13 (myeloid markers) to remove myeloid contaminants, followed by re-training SAE on purified erythroid population to determine if this feature resolves or persists

programme_name: Plasma cell immunoglobulin synthesis and ER stress
functional_description: This feature represents a plasma cell-specific programme centred on immunoglobulin heavy and light chain production (IGHD, IGKV2-29, IGLV2-18, IGLL5) coupled with endoplasmic reticulum protein folding and quality control mechanisms. The co-expression of FKBP11, FKBP2 (prolyl isomerases), SSR4 (translocon component), DERL3 (ER-associated degradation), and SELENOM (redox-active selenoprotein) indicates active management of ER proteostasis during the massive secretory load of antibody synthesis.
key_evidence: IGHD, IGKV2-29, IGLV2-18, IGLL5: Core immunoglobulin variable and constant region components diagnostic of plasma cell differentiation
FKBP11, FKBP2: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerases essential for proper folding of immunoglobulin domains in the ER lumen
SSR4: Signal sequence receptor subunit mediating co-translational translocation of nascent immunoglobulins across the ER membrane
DERL3: ER-resident derlin involved in retro-translocation of misfolded proteins for proteasomal degradation
MZB1: Marginal zone B cell maturation factor supporting plasma cell differentiation and proliferation
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence of sorted plasma cells (CD138+) showing co-localization of immunoglobulin light/heavy chains with FKBP11 and BiP (ER chaperone) in perinuclear ER; validate by blocking prolyl isomerase activity (FK506) and measuring immunoglobulin secretion capacity.

programme_name: Megakaryocyte contamination and platelet adhesion
functional_description: This feature represents aberrant megakaryocyte and platelet-related gene expression in early erythroid progenitors, driven by integrin signaling (ITGA2B), von Willebrand factor secretion (VWF), and calcium-dependent mechanotransduction (TRPC6, STUM). The gene set reflects either genuine megakaryocyte precursor contamination in the cluster (11.5% of activating cells) or cross-lineage expression of hemostatic genes during early erythroid differentiation, inconsistent with canonical early erythroid metabolism.
key_evidence: ITGA2B: megakaryocyte-specific integrin alpha 2b chain, not typically expressed in erythroid lineage
VWF: von Willebrand factor synthesis and secretion marker of megakaryocytes and endothelial cells, absent in erythroid differentiation
MMRN1: platelet and endothelial multimerin, incompatible with erythroid metabolism programme
TRPC6: calcium influx channel activated by diacylglycerol, involved in platelet activation rather than erythroid maturation
ITGA2B + VWF + MMRN1: co-expression pattern is diagnostic of megakaryocytic lineage, not erythroid progenitors
suggested_validation: Sort cluster 3 cells by ITGA2B and VWF expression using flow cytometry to confirm megakaryocyte contamination; perform CD41/CD61 gating to separate megakaryocyte precursors and validate that erythroid-only subsets lack this transcriptional programme.

programme_name: Plasma cell contamination in erythroid sorting
functional_description: This feature represents a B cell/plasma cell transcriptional programme dominated by immunoglobulin gene expression (IGLC7, IGLV variants, IGHG3) and B cell receptor signaling components (CD79A). The 2.5% plasma cell contamination in the top 200 activating cells, combined with the complete absence of erythroid-specific genes (globin, heme biosynthesis, or mitochondrial bioenergetics markers), indicates this is a technical artifact rather than a genuine erythroid differentiation stage.
key_evidence: IGLC7, IGLV1-41, IGLV3-21, IGLV5-48, IGLV6-57, IGLV1-51: Immunoglobulin constant and variable regions incompatible with erythroid lineage
CD79A: B cell receptor signaling component absent in erythroid cells
IGHG3: Immunoglobulin heavy chain constant region, diagnostic of B cell/plasma cell origin
MZB1: Marginal zone B cell-specific protein with no erythroid function
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry re-sorting of basophilic and pro-erythroblasts with plasma cell marker exclusion (CD138-, CD19-), followed by RNA-seq to confirm absence of Ig genes and presence of erythroid-specific programmes (GATA1 targets, globin, ALAS2, mitochondrial complexes)

programme_name: Plasma cell contamination in erythroid sorting
functional_description: This feature represents aberrant immunoglobulin heavy and light chain gene expression (IGHG4, IGHV3-53/13/66, IGLL5) co-occurring with erythroid cells, indicating either plasma cell contamination in the basophilic erythroblast population or dual transcriptional activity. The presence of ER-resident proteins (LAMP5, DERL3) and lysosomal proteins (ATP10B) suggests activation of secretory pathway machinery atypical for early erythroid differentiation, which normally prioritises ribosomal and haemoglobin synthesis.
key_evidence: IGHG4, IGHV3-53/13/66: immunoglobulin constant and variable regions exclusively expressed in B/plasma cells, not erythroid lineage
IGLL5: surrogate light chain component diagnostic of B cell compartment; absent in erythroid differentiation
LAMP5, DERL3: ER-Golgi trafficking machinery consistent with antibody secretion pathway, not erythroid protein synthesis
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting with CD138 (plasma cell marker) and glycophorin A (erythroid marker) to physically separate populations before RNA-seq, confirming whether immunoglobulin genes cluster with bona fide plasma cells or represent genuine dual-programme erythroid cells

programme_name: Aberrant immunoglobulin expression in erythroid progenitors
functional_description: This feature represents ectopic activation of B-cell immunoglobulin gene segments (heavy and lambda variable regions, IGHM, JCHAIN) in early erythroid progenitors, accompanied by secretory pathway machinery (SEC11C, RAB30). This is likely a spurious transcriptional programme or represents rare B-cell contamination rather than a genuine erythroid differentiation stage. The presence of EPB41L4B and BHLHE41 suggests attempted erythroid identity, but immunoglobulin expression is functionally incompatible with erythroid development.
key_evidence: IGHM, IGHV2-5, IGHV3-64D, IGLV1-44: Complete B-cell receptor gene expression inappropriate in erythroid lineage
JCHAIN: Joining chain for multimeric immunoglobulin assembly—definitively marks plasma cell/B-cell programme
SEC11C, RAB30: Secretory pathway components required for antibody synthesis, not erythroid function
suggested_validation: Sort basophilic erythroblasts and pro-erythroblasts by flow cytometry (CD71+, CD45−, CD19−) and perform RNA-FISH or qPCR to verify whether immunoglobulin transcripts co-localize with genuine erythroid markers (KLF1, GATA1, EPB41) or represent a distinct contaminating B-cell population.

programme_name: Plasma cell immunoglobulin secretory pathway
functional_description: This feature represents active immunoglobulin heavy and light chain synthesis coupled with endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein translocation and quality control mechanisms. The programme is driven by immunoglobulin gene expression (IGHG1/3/4, IGLC3, IGHV segments) combined with translocon machinery (SSR4), ER stress response components (HERPUD1), and protein folding catalysts (FKBP11). The 7.5% plasma cell composition and dominance of Ig genes indicates this feature captures antibody secretory differentiation rather than erythroid bioenergetics.
key_evidence: IGHG1/IGHG3/IGHG4: Immunoglobulin constant regions indicating active B-cell plasma cell differentiation
IGLC3: Immunoglobulin lambda light chain required for complete antibody assembly
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein complex for ER-to-secretory pathway translocation
HERPUD1: ER stress response and unfolded protein response (UPR) activation during high-volume antibody synthesis
FKBP11: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase facilitating proline-rich Ig domain folding
suggested_validation: Perform co-immunofluorescence staining of top-200 activating cells for CD138 (plasma cell marker) and intracellular immunoglobulin (IgG), combined with flow cytometry sorting to quantify the true plasma cell percentage and correlate with SAE feature activation scores.

programme_name: Plasma cell immunoglobulin synthesis programme
functional_description: This feature captures the antibody production and secretion machinery of plasma cells, characterized by heavy and light chain immunoglobulin genes (IGHV, IGHA2, IGLV variants) and the joining chain (JCHAIN) required for multimeric IgA/IgM assembly. Supporting genes include ER protein folding machinery (PDIA4) for immunoglobulin processing and TNF-receptor superfamily members (TNFRSF17, CD27, TNFRSF13B) that regulate plasma cell survival and differentiation signals.
key_evidence: IGHV3-64, IGHV3-30: Variable domain antigen-binding regions for immunoglobulin specificity
IGHA2: Constant alpha domain essential for IgA isotype function and mucosal immunity
JCHAIN: Covalent joining of IgA/IgM dimers and polymers required for secretion
PDIA4: ER protein disulfide isomerase enabling heavy/light chain folding and assembly
TNFRSF17, CD27, TNFRSF13B: TNF-R superfamily members providing survival signals and plasma cell homing (CCR10)
suggested_validation: The erythroid cell contamination (85.5% erythroblasts) suggests this feature may represent plasma cells captured within the erythroid cluster. Validate by performing flow cytometry sorting of CD138+ plasma cells from the BoneMarrowMap tissue and re-analyzing SAE activation patterns in pure plasma cell populations, or by examining whether this feature shows strong negative correlation with mature erythroid markers (HBA, HBB, GYPA).

programme_name: Plasma cell antibody synthesis and ER quality control
functional_description: This feature represents the integrated secretory pathway programme in antibody-producing plasma cells, characterized by heavy reliance on endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein synthesis, translocation, and quality control. The programme couples immunoglobulin heavy and light chain transcription (IGHG1, IGHV3-33, IGLV2-14, IGLV3-21, IGLL5) with ER translocon function (SSR4), protein folding assistance (FKBP11), and ER-associated degradation (DERL3, XBP1). XBP1 activation indicates active unfolded protein response (UPR) signalling, essential for managing the exceptional protein synthesis load in plasma cells.
key_evidence: IGHG1, IGHV3-33, IGLV2-14: Immunoglobulin gene segments encoding variable and constant regions for antibody production
SSR4: Translocon-associated protein complex component for co-translational protein translocation into ER lumen
XBP1: Master transcriptional regulator of UPR and ER stress response; activated by ATF6 signalling to expand ER capacity
DERL3: ER-resident derlin mediating retrotranslocation of misfolded proteins for proteasomal degradation
FKBP11: Peptidyl-prolyl isomerase facilitating proper folding of proline-rich immunoglobulin chains
suggested_validation: Measure XBP1 splicing (XBP1s/XBP1u ratio by qPCR) and ATF6 nuclear translocation by flow cytometry in sorted plasma cells vs erythroblasts to confirm UPR activation; correlate with immunoglobulin secretion rates by ELISA or intracellular staining.

programme_name: Plasma cell contamination in erythroid sorting
functional_description: This feature does not represent an erythroid mitochondrial biogenesis programme. Instead, it captures a plasma cell transcriptional signature contaminating the early erythroid population, dominated by immunoglobulin genes (IGLV3-27, IGLL5, JCHAIN, MZB1) and B-cell markers (CCR10). The presence of CCND1 suggests proliferative plasma cell precursors, while SLC22A17 indicates iron/siderophore handling in antibody-secreting cells.
key_evidence: IGLV3-27: immunoglobulin lambda variable gene; plasma cell-specific transcription
IGLL5: immunoglobulin lambda-like polypeptide; B-lineage marker unrelated to erythroid differentiation
JCHAIN: joining chain of multimeric immunoglobulins; hallmark of plasma cell antibody secretion
MZB1: marginal zone B cell protein; B-cell lineage commitment marker
CCR10: chemokine receptor mediating plasma cell homing; absent in erythroid cells

functional_description: This feature represents a coordinated programme of immunoglobulin production and secretion active in a minor plasma cell population within the erythroid-enriched cluster. The dominant genes encode immunoglobulin heavy and light chains (IGHV3-64, IGHV3-30, IGHA2, JCHAIN), plus ER protein-folding machinery (PDIA4) required for antibody assembly and secretion. programme_name: Immunoglobulin pseudogene expression artifact
functional_description: This feature appears to capture spurious immunoglobulin gene expression (IGLVI-70, IGHG3, IGHV3-72, IGHV3-23) in early erythroid progenitors, likely representing technical artifacts such as ambient RNA contamination or doublet detection. The presence of immunoglobulin heavy and light chain genes in a basophilic erythroblast-dominant population (47%) contradicts the canonical erythroid differentiation programme and suggests contamination from plasma cells (1% stated but likely underestimated in localized sequencing regions).

programme_name: Plasma cell immunoglobulin contamination artifact
functional_description: This feature represents a technical artifact dominated by immunoglobulin gene expression (IGLV2-34, IGLL5, IGLL1, IGLV2-14, IGHG2, IGHV4-55) that is inconsistent with early erythroid biology. functional_description: This feature represents contaminating plasma cell transcripts rather than a genuine erythroid programme. The dominance of immunoglobulin genes (IGHA2, JCHAIN), B-cell receptor signalling components (BLK, TNFRSF13B, TNFRSF18), and lymphocyte-specific markers despite 95.5% erythroid cell annotation indicates either technical contamination or a small but transcriptionally dominant plasma cell population. The presence of SPACA3 and unannotated long non-coding RNAs further suggests data quality issues rather than coherent erythroid biology.

functional_description: This feature does not represent an erythroid bioenergetics programme. The top genes encode immunoglobulin light and heavy chains, characteristic of antibody-secreting cells rather than mitochondrial bioenergetics machinery.

functional_description: This programme coordinates early erythroid proliferation through mitotic checkpoint control and cell cycle progression machinery. functional_description: This programme coordinates the final enzymatic steps of heme biosynthesis (ferrochelatase, uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase, hydroxymethylbilane synthase) with iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis (GLRX5) and mitochondrial iron transport (SLC25A39, TMEM14C). functional_description: This feature represents coordinated upregulation of mitochondrial structural and bioenergetic proteins in early erythroid differentiation, specifically ATP synthase subunits (ATP5A1, ATP5B, ATP5C1, ATP5F1, ATP5G1/G3), mitochondrial import machinery (TIMM10), and mitochondrial translation machinery (MRPS17). functional_description: This programme coordinates the terminal steps of heme biosynthesis with mitochondrial iron-sulfur (Fe-S) cluster assembly during basophilic erythroblast maturation. functional_description: This programme represents the early erythroid expansion phase characterized by MYC-mediated cell cycle progression and rapid protein synthesis capacity.
