BLVRB: Biliverdin reductase—final enzymatic step in heme catabolism/recycling, indicating active heme turnover
MPC2: Mitochondrial pyruvate carrier—fuels mitochondrial metabolism during metabolic reprogramming
SOD1: Superoxide dismutase—mitigates ROS from elevated oxidative phosphorylation in early erythroid cells
TMEM14C: Predicted mitochondrial transporter—coordinates mitochondrial biogenesis during erythroid differentiation
suggested_validation: Quantify mitochondrial mass (MitoTracker) and heme synthesis rate (fluorescent heme precursor incorporation) across FACS-sorted pro-erythroblast, basophilic, and polychromatic erythroblast stages, correlating with SAE feature activation scores.

programme_name: Ribosomal biogenesis and mitochondrial oxidative capacity
functional_description: This programme coordinates assembly of cytoplasmic ribosomes (40S and 60S subunits) with upregulation of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation complexes (NADH dehydrogenase, cytochrome c oxidase) in early pro-erythroblasts. This coupling reflects the massive biosynthetic and energetic demands of early erythroid progenitors, which must simultaneously synthesize ribosomal machinery for subsequent globin translation while generating ATP to fuel rapid cell division and anabolic pathways.
key_evidence: RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0, RPS23, RPS17, RPS24, RPS2: structural components of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunits required for ribosome assembly
MT-ND1, MT-CO2, MT-CO3: mitochondrial electron transport chain subunits that generate the proton gradient for ATP synthesis
EEF1B2: guanine nucleotide exchange factor enabling efficient translation elongation once ribosomes are assembled
NPM1: nucleophosmin mediates ribosomal protein chaperoning and ribosome assembly in the nucleolus
suggested_validation: Perform active mitochondrial staining (TMRM or MitoTracker) combined with ribosome quantification (metabolic labelling with puromycin or polysome profiling) in flow-sorted pro-erythroblasts versus later erythroid stages to confirm coordinated upregulation of mitochondrial capacity and ribosomal biogenesis.

programme_name: Glycolytic metabolism in proliferating erythroid progenitors
functional_description: This feature represents a metabolic programme centred on glycolytic ATP generation and translational machinery support in actively cycling erythroid and myeloid progenitors. The co-expression of glycolytic enzymes (ENO1, GAPDH), translation factors (EEF1B2), and ribosomal proteins (RPS24) indicates coordination of energy metabolism with protein synthesis capacity during rapid cell division. The presence of CD34 and IGFBP7 suggests progenitor self-renewal signals alongside metabolic activation.
key_evidence: ENO1: glycolysis rate-limiting enzyme for ATP production in proliferating cells
GAPDH: central glycolytic enzyme; also reported in cell cycle progression
RPS24: ribosomal protein essential for translation during high biosynthetic demand
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor required for efficient protein synthesis in cycling cells
CD34: stem/progenitor cell marker enriched in CFU-E and cycling progenitors
IGFBP7: growth factor signalling molecule supporting progenitor maintenance
suggested_validation: Measure glycolytic flux (lactate production, glucose consumption) and protein synthesis rates (puromycin incorporation) in sorted CFU-E and cycling progenitor populations, comparing high vs. low expressers of this feature signature

programme_name: Ribosome biogenesis and translational capacity establishment
functional_description: This programme represents coordinated upregulation of ribosomal protein components (40S and 60S subunits) and translation elongation factors during pro-erythroblast proliferation and early basophilic erythroblast transition. The co-expression of structural ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPS23, RPL4, RPL7A, RPL37A) with translation machinery components (EEF1B2) reflects massive ribosome assembly required to support the imminent high-volume globin synthesis phase of erythroid differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS23, RPS17, RPS24: 40S ribosomal subunit assembly during G1/S transition in early erythroblasts
RPL4, RPL7A, RPL37A, RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit maturation prerequisite for translation initiation
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor GEF activity enabling ribosome translocation for sustained protein synthesis
NPM1: Nucleolar protein chaperoning ribosomal protein assembly and biogenesis coordination
SLC25A3: Mitochondrial phosphate import supporting ATP production for ribosome assembly (energetic demand)
YBX1, HNRNPA1: RNA chaperones facilitating pre-rRNA processing and ribosomal protein mRNA stabilization
suggested_validation: Perform polysome profiling (sucrose gradient fractionation) and qRT-PCR for 18S/28S rRNA on sorted pro-erythroblasts vs mature erythroblasts to quantify ribosome assembly capacity and correlate with SAE feature activity scores
prior_programme_name: Early erythroblast translational and metabolic activation

programme_name: 40S/60S ribosomal protein synthesis assembly
functional_description: This feature captures the coordinated expression of structural ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A) alongside translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) and ribosome assembly chaperones (NPM1), defining the core translational machinery assembly programme essential for rapid protein synthesis in erythroid progenitors. The strong CFU-E and Pro-Erythroblast enrichment indicates this programme is maximal during the proliferative-to-maturation transition when cells require massive capacity for hemoglobin synthesis. Concurrent expression of glycolytic enzymes (GAPDH, ENO1) and the protease inhibitor SERPINB1 supports ribosome protection during active translation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A: structural components of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunits required for ribosome assembly
EEF1B2: guanine nucleotide exchange factor essential for elongation factor recycling during translation cycles
NPM1: nucleophosmin acts as ribosome biogenesis chaperone and nucleolar organizer critical for pre-rRNA processing
GAPDH, ENO1: glycolytic enzymes provide ATP and metabolic precursors for ribosome synthesis during proliferation
SERPINB1: serine protease inhibitor protects ribosomal machinery from proteolysis during active translation
suggested_validation: Perform polysome profiling on sorted CFU-E and Pro-Erythroblast populations to quantify active translation capacity and correlate with feature activation levels; combine with qPCR validation of RPS24/RPS23/RPL37A co-expression kinetics during in vitro erythroid differentiation

programme_name: Oxidative phosphorylation coupled mitochondrial translation
functional_description: This programme coordinates early erythroid cells' mitochondrial bioenergetic capacity through concurrent activation of electron transport chain (ETC) subunits and mitochondrial ribosomal proteins. The co-expression of MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, and MT-ND5 (core ETC complexes I and IV) with 60S mitochondrial ribosomal components (RPL37A, RPL7A, RPLP0) reflects the requirement for de novo synthesis of hydrophobic ETC subunits encoded by mtDNA during the massive expansion of mitochondrial mass in pro-erythroblasts. This is distinct from cytoplasmic translation programmes, supporting the energetic demands of haem biosynthesis and iron import.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-CO3: cytochrome c oxidase catalytic core for terminal electron transport
MT-ND1, MT-ND5: Complex I NADH oxidation, primary source of proton-motive force
RPL37A, RPL7A, RPLP0: mitochondrial-specific ribosomal subunits for ETC subunit translation
UQCRH: Complex III ubiquinone-cytochrome c interface, electron relay between complexes
EEF1B2: translation elongation in mitochondrial translation machinery
suggested_validation: Co-immunoprecipitation of mtDNA-encoded COX subunits with mitochondrial ribosomes (MRPL markers) in pro-erythroblasts, or pulse-labelling with ³⁵S-methionine to quantify de novo mitochondrial protein synthesis rates across erythroid differentiation stages.

programme_name: Mitochondrial OXPHOS assembly in megakaryocytic commitment
functional_description: This feature captures coordinated expression of mitochondrial electron transport chain subunits (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5) alongside megakaryocyte-lineage markers (ITGA2B, CD63, PLEK), indicating active oxidative phosphorylation capacity during megakaryocytic differentiation rather than erythroid maturation. The substantial megakaryocyte precursor representation (23.5%) and presence of platelet-associated proteins suggests this programme functions in megakaryocytes undergoing mitochondrial energetic priming, not erythroid progenitors as previously annotated.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5: Core OXPHOS subunits defining electron transport chain assembly and ATP generation capacity
ITGA2B: Megakaryocyte-specific integrin essential for platelet formation and megakaryocytic commitment
CD63, PLEK, PDLIM1: Tetraspanin and platelet-associated proteins indicating megakaryocytic rather than erythroid differentiation state
TMSB4X: Cytoskeletal regulator required for megakaryocyte cytoplasmic extension and proplatelet formation
suggested_validation: Perform mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM/JC-1) staining and oxygen consumption rate (Seahorse) analysis comparing isolated megakaryocyte precursors vs. CFU-E cells to confirm OXPHOS elevation is megakaryocyte-specific rather than general progenitor biology.

programme_name: Ribosome biogenesis and mitochondrial OXPHOS
functional_description: This programme coordinates the assembly of translational machinery (ribosomal proteins RPS2, RPS23, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0) with mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (MT-ND1, MT-ND5, MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH) in early erythroid progenitors. The co-activation of both ribosomal protein synthesis and OXPHOS components reflects the exceptional energetic and biosynthetic demands of erythroid differentiation, where rapid hemoglobin synthesis requires both abundant ribosomes and ATP generation to support the massive translational load.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS23, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0: core 40S/60S ribosomal subunit proteins required for ribosome assembly and translational capacity
MT-ND1, MT-ND5, MT-CO2, MT-CO3, UQCRH: mitochondrial electron transport chain and oxidative phosphorylation—essential for ATP supply to power ribosome function and globin synthesis
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor mediating GTP-dependent ribosomal translocation, directly coupling ribosome activity to energy availability
suggested_validation: Perform single-cell metabolomics or Seahorse XF analysis on sorted Pro-Erythroblasts and CFU-Es to demonstrate concurrent elevation of ATP production and mitochondrial function in cells activating this feature; confirm ribosome assembly by negative stain EM or polysome profiling of these cells versus mature erythroblasts.

programme_name: Ribosome biogenesis and translational capacity
functional_description: This programme coordinates the assembly and maturation of ribosomal subunits with the expansion of translational machinery capacity during early erythroid commitment. The feature is driven by coordinated expression of ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S components), ribosomal RNA processing factors (FBL), and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), reflecting the bioenergetic demand of haemoglobin synthesis initiation in CFU-E and pro-erythroblast stages.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPS23, RPS24, RPS17, RPL7A, RPL4, RPL37A, RPLP0: structural components of ribosomal 40S and 60S subunits required for assembly and catalytic activity
FBL: nucleolar rRNA 2'-O-methyltransferase essential for pre-rRNA processing and ribosome maturation
EEF1B2: guanine nucleotide exchange factor for elongation factor delivery during translation initiation and elongation
IMPDH2: rate-limiting enzyme in GTP biosynthesis required to fuel ribosome assembly and translational initiation in proliferating progenitors
NPM1: nucleolar chaperone involved in ribosome assembly and protein chaperoning during ribosomal biogenesis
suggested_validation: Quantify ribosomal RNA transcription rates and 40S/60S subunit abundance using sucrose gradient sedimentation in sorted CFU-E vs mature erythroblasts, correlating with SAE feature activation strength.

programme_name: Ribosomal protein synthesis and translation elongation
functional_description: This programme coordinates the expression of ribosomal structural proteins (RPS17, RPS23, RPS24, RPL37A) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) in proliferating erythroid progenitors undergoing rapid haemoglobin synthesis. The programme supports the massive protein synthesis demand during erythroid differentiation, where ribosomes must be assembled and functional to sustain high-rate globin chain translation.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS23, RPS17: structural components of ribosomal 40S subunit required for mRNA decoding during active translation
RPL37A: structural component of ribosomal 60S subunit essential for peptide bond formation
EEF1B2: guanine nucleotide exchange factor that facilitates translational elongation cycle and ribosome recycling
HNRNPA1/HNRNPA1L2: RNA-binding proteins regulating mRNA processing and ribosomal protein mRNA transport to support coordinated ribosome assembly
suggested_validation: Measure ribosomal content (flow cytometry staining with anti-RPS6 or anti-RPL22 antibodies) and protein synthesis rates (pulse-chase with puromycin or O-propargyl-puromycin) in CFU-E vs. non-erythroid progenitors to confirm ribosome-dependent translation capacity correlates with this feature activity.

programme_name: Early erythroid progenitor translational programme
Oxidative phosphorylation complex assembly
functional_description: This feature captures coordinated expression of core subunits from respiratory complexes I, III, and IV (NADH dehydrogenase, cytochrome bc1, and cytochrome c oxidase), along with mitochondrial import machinery and nucleotide metabolism enzymes. This programme is active primarily in pro-erythroblasts and CFU-Es, reflecting the massive ATP demand during early erythroid proliferation before terminal maturation shifts metabolism to glycolysis.
key_evidence: MT-ND1, MT-ND5: Complex I NADH dehydrogenase subunits enabling electron entry into the respiratory chain
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, COX5A: Complex IV cytochrome c oxidase subunits catalysing terminal oxygen reduction
UQCRH, UQCRQ: Complex III ubiquinol-cytochrome c reductase subunits completing the electron transfer chain
TIMM13: Mitochondrial translocase for inner membrane protein import, required to build respiratory complexes
NME1: Nucleoside diphosphate kinase replenishing ATP and GTP for biosynthetic demands during proliferation
TPI1: Glycolytic enzyme supporting ATP regeneration alongside oxidative phosphorylation
suggested_validation: Measure oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and ATP production in sorted pro-erythroblasts vs. later-stage erythroblasts by Seahorse mito stress test; correlate with mitochondrial mass and complex I-IV protein levels by flow cytometry or immunofluorescence.

programme_name: pDC type I interferon and cytotoxic response
functional_description: This feature represents a specialized immune activation programme combining plasmacytoid dendritic cell (pDC) identity markers with cytotoxic and inflammatory effector functions. The programme is driven by pDC-specific genes (LILRA4, SPIB) alongside granzyme/perforin-mediated cytotoxicity (GZMB), NK cell receptors (KLRB1), and inflammatory cytokine signalling (IL32, LTB), consistent with activated pDCs transitioning toward antiviral type I IFN and cytotoxic effector responses.
key_evidence: LILRA4: pDC-specific immunoglobulin receptor, defines plasmacytoid dendritic cell identity
SPIB: PU-box transcription factor central to pDC lineage commitment and activation
GZMB: serine protease for cytotoxic granule-mediated killing, atypical but present in activated pDCs
KLRB1: NK receptor expression indicating NK-like cytotoxic priming in pDC subset
IL32: pro-inflammatory cytokine supporting pDC antiviral response amplification
LTB: TNF family member enabling lymphoid activation and secondary immune signalling
suggested_validation: Sort pDCs from bone marrow by LILRA4+SPIB+ expression and perform RNA-seq with intracellular staining for granzyme B and IFN-α/β to confirm activated pDC identity and type I IFN secretion capacity in response to TLR9 agonist stimulation.

programme_name: MHC-II antigen presentation machinery assembly
functional_description: This programme coordinately activates the complete MHC-II presentation pathway in cDC1s and pre-cDCs, including expression of HLA-DR, HLA-DP, and HLA-DQ heterodimeric components alongside CD74 chaperone and HLA-DM peptide-loading machinery. The co-expression of invariant chain (CD74) with all three MHC-II isotype pairs indicates active assembly of stable, peptide-receptive MHC-II complexes required for professional antigen presentation.
key_evidence: CD74: invariant chain chaperone essential for MHC-II folding and peptide compartmentalization
HLA-DRA/DRB1/DRB5: complete HLA-DR isotype expression (α and β chains) indicating functional heterodimer assembly
HLA-DMA/DMB: peptide exchange catalyst that facilitates loading of high-affinity peptides into MHC-II grooves
HLA-DPA1/DPB1 + HLA-DQA1/DQB1: parallel expression of DP and DQ isotypes enabling multiple presentation pathways
CST3 + GSTP1: oxidative and proteolytic stress resistance supporting sustained antigen processing capacity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantification of surface MHC-II-peptide complex density (using allotype-specific antibodies) combined with peptide-binding assays on sorted cDC1s from feature-high vs. feature-low populations, or functional presentation assay using labelled peptide-MHC-II tetramers.

programme_name: HLA-II peptide loading and antigen presentation
functional_description: This programme coordinates expression of HLA class II heterodimer components (DP, DQ, DR families) along with the peptide-exchange machinery (HLA-DM) and chaperone CD74, enabling professional antigen presentation by cDC1 and cDC2. The inclusion of CD1C and CLEC10A suggests integration with lipid and glycan presentation pathways characteristic of mature dendritic cells.
key_evidence: HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1: DP heterodimer assembly for peptide presentation
HLA-DRA/HLA-DRB1/HLA-DRB5: DR heterodimer formation across multiple alleles
HLA-DMA/HLA-DMB: peptide-exchange catalyst for MHC-II loading optimization
CD74: chaperone ensuring proper HLA-II folding and trafficking
CD1C: lipid antigen presentation on dendritic cells
CLEC10A: pattern recognition for glycan-bearing antigens
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry measuring surface HLA-DR/DP/DQ expression combined with biochemical assay of peptide-loaded vs unloaded MHC-II complexes in sorted cDC1 vs cDC2 subsets, or functional presentation assay using peptide-pulsed DCs and CD4+ T cell recognition.

programme_name: Antimicrobial innate immunity and damage-associated signalling
functional_description: This feature captures a coordinated innate immune programme in classical monocytes centred on secreted and cytoplasmic antimicrobial effectors (S100A8/A9/A12 calprotectin complex, lysozyme, ribonucleases, ficolin) combined with damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) signalling (granulin, resistin, versican) and pattern recognition receptor signalling (TYROBP/DAP12). This represents the mature classical monocyte's role in bacterial containment and alarmin-mediated inflammatory amplification rather than differentiation per se.
key_evidence: S100A8/A9/A12: form the calprotectin heterocomplex—a key antimicrobial and pro-inflammatory DAMP with metal-chelating and bacteriostatic properties
LYZ + RNASE2: secreted antimicrobial hydrolases targeting bacterial cell wall and RNA
FCN1 + TYROBP: pattern recognition receptors and ITAM-bearing adaptor enabling bacterial sensing and immune activation
GRN + RETN + VCAN: secreted alarmin-like molecules that amplify inflammatory responses and tissue remodelling
MNDA + CD14: lineage-specific markers confirming monocyte identity with CD14-mediated LPS co-recognition
suggested_validation: Stimulate CD14+ monocytes with bacterial LPS or lipoteichoic acid (TLR ligands) and measure coordinated upregulation of calprotectin release (ELISA for S100A8/A9), lysozyme activity, and granulin secretion via immunoassay; confirm TYROBP-dependent signalling dependency using CRISPR knockdown of DAP12.

programme_name: CD16+ monocyte phagocytic and antimicrobial programme
functional_description: This feature captures the lysosomal protease and phagocytic machinery characteristic of CD16+ non-classical monocytes. The programme coordinates expression of cathepsin S (CTSS) and other lysosomal hydrolases (PSAP), actin-remodeling proteins (AIF1, COTL1) for cytoskeletal dynamics, and ITAM-signaling adaptors (TYROBP, FCER1G) that drive pattern recognition and antibody-dependent cellular responses. This reflects the enhanced antimicrobial and tissue-surveillance capacity of CD16+ monocytes relative to classical CD14+ monocytes.
key_evidence: CTSS: lysosomal cysteine protease essential for intracellular pathogen degradation
AIF1: calcium-actin binding protein promoting inflammatory macrophage activation
TYROBP: ITAM adaptor mediating Fc receptor signaling and pathogen recognition
PSAP: lysosomal protease cofactor and lipid antigen presentation
COTL1: F-actin regulator enabling cytoskeletal remodeling for phagocytosis
CD68: pan-monocyte/macrophage marker reflective of phagocytic identity
suggested_validation: Perform flow cytometry sorting of CD16+CD14- monocytes and measure CTSS activity and cathepsin S protein levels by Western blot and immunofluorescence; correlate with phagocytic capacity assays using opsonized pathogens or beads.

programme_name: Myeloid lysosomal proteolysis and iron handling
functional_description: This programme coordinates lysosomal cathepsin activity (CTSS), intracellular iron storage (FTH1), and actin remodeling in professional phagocytes. The co-expression of proteolytic enzymes, iron metabolism genes, and actin-binding proteins reflects the specialized capacity of CD16+ monocytes and cDC2 cells to process internalized pathogens and manage iron from phagocytosed material—a distinct sub-programme within myeloid activation that emphasizes intracellular degradation over surface antigen presentation.
key_evidence: CTSS: Lysosomal cysteine protease essential for pathogen degradation in phagolysosomes
FTH1: Iron storage capacity needed to sequester labile iron from heme and prevent bacterial utilization
SAT1: Polyamine catabolism regulates inflammatory responses and antimicrobial defence in myeloid cells
TYROBP: ITAM-signaling adaptor coupling Fc and TLR receptors to phagocytic activation
S100A4/A6: Calcium-responsive regulators of actin dynamics during phagolysosome formation and migration
AIF1: Actin-binding protein induced by inflammatory cytokines to support myeloid effector functions
suggested_validation: Quantify lysosomal proteolytic activity (cathepsin S substrate cleavage assay) and iron accumulation (ferrozine-based iron quantification) in flow-sorted CD16+ monocytes vs. CD14+ monocytes, with functional inhibition of FTH1 or CTSS to assess impact on intracellular bacterial killing.

programme_name: Myeloid-megakaryocyte transdifferentiation with platelet protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature captures a hybrid transcriptional state where classical monocytes co-express megakaryocyte-lineage genes, particularly platelet structural proteins (GP9, PF4, PLEK) alongside myeloid innate immune mediators (S100A8/A9/A12, LCN2). The presence of actin-regulatory proteins (TMSB4X, GSN, ZYX) and TREML1 suggests active cytoskeletal remodelling concurrent with megakaryocyte priming, consistent with documented monocyte-megakaryocyte plasticity in bone marrow stress responses.
key_evidence: GP9 & PF4: megakaryocyte-restricted platelet glycoproteins aberrantly expressed in CD14+ monocytes (25% cluster composition)
S100A8/A9/A12: canonical myeloid danger-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) for neutrophil recruitment and monocyte priming
PLEK & ZYX: focal adhesion and cytoskeletal proteins enabling rapid morphological plasticity during transdifferentiation
TREML1: myeloid immune checkpoint receptor absent in mature megakaryocytes, confirming hybrid progenitor state
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining CD14+GP9+ monocyte subset with EdU incorporation and quantitative RNA-FISH for simultaneous S100A8 and PF4 single-cell expression to confirm transdifferentiating intermediate identity independent of doublet artefact.

programme_name: Megakaryocyte cytoskeletal and granule biogenesis
functional_description: This feature captures the megakaryocyte-specific transcriptional programme focused on cytoskeletal reorganisation and alpha-granule protein synthesis. The dominant expression in basophilic and pro-erythroblasts likely reflects the bipotent erythro-megakaryocytic progenitor state where megakaryocytic commitment genes (PPBP, PF4, MYL9) are being co-activated alongside cytoskeletal remodelling machinery (CALD1, SAMD14, ILK). This programme is distinct from erythroid-specific processes and represents early megakaryocytic lineage specification within the common erythro-megakaryocytic progenitor compartment.
key_evidence: PPBP: megakaryocyte-specific alpha-granule protein and CXC chemokine
PF4: platelet factor 4, canonical alpha-granule cargo released from activated megakaryocytes
MYL9: myosin light chain essential for megakaryocytic cytoplasmic maturation and platelet extension
CALD1: actin-binding protein regulating smooth muscle-like contraction during megakaryocyte maturation
SAMD14: actin filament organisation protein supporting cytoskeletal remodelling
ILK: integrin-linked kinase mediating cytoskeletal signalling during megakaryocytic commitment
suggested_validation: Sort basophilic erythroblasts and pro-erythroblasts by CD41 (platelet integrin) expression and perform RNA-seq comparing CD41+ (megakaryocytic-committed) versus CD41− (erythroid-committed) populations to confirm PPBP/PF4/MYL9 enrichment in the megakaryocytic branch despite erythroid morphology.

programme_name: Heme biosynthesis and mitochondrial iron-sulphur biogenesis
functional_description: This programme coordinates heme synthesis and iron-sulphur cluster assembly in erythroid and megakaryocytic progenitors. It encompasses terminal heme metabolism (BLVRB, UROD), heme trafficking (HEBP1), iron-sulphur cluster biogenesis (GLRX5), and mitochondrial integrity (VDAC3, TMEM14C), alongside antioxidant protection (PRDX2, SOD1) needed to manage oxidative stress from haem synthesis intermediates.
key_evidence: BLVRB: catalyses final step of heme metabolism (biliverdin reduction)
UROD: heme biosynthetic pathway enzyme (uroporphyrinogen decarboxylation)
GLRX5: mitochondrial iron-sulphur cluster biogenesis essential for erythroid differentiation
HEBP1: intracellular heme binding and trafficking protein
VDAC3: mitochondrial porin required for metabolite transport during haem synthesis
PRDX2, SOD1: antioxidant enzymes mitigating haem intermediate-induced oxidative stress
suggested_validation: Quantify intracellular haem levels and iron-sulphur cluster content in basophilic erythroblasts with SAE feature 51 high vs low activation using mass spectrometry or fluorescent haem biosynthetic intermediates; correlate with feature expression levels.

programme_name: G2/M checkpoint and mitotic spindle assembly
functional_description: This programme coordinates the transition through G2/M phase checkpoint and assembly of the mitotic spindle apparatus. The signature combines microtubule polymerization machinery (TUBA1B, TUBB), mitotic checkpoint regulators (STMN1 as a microtubule-destabilizing catastrophe factor), and chromatin remodeling factors (HMGN1, HMGN2, HMGB1) that facilitate chromosome condensation and segregation. The enrichment in Large Pre-B cells reflects the high proliferative demand of lymphoid progenitors undergoing rapid cell cycle progression.
key_evidence: STMN1: microtubule destabilization and dynamic instability during mitotic spindle checkpoint control
TUBA1B, TUBB: core constituents of mitotic spindle microtubule polymer assembly
HMGN1, HMGN2: nucleosomal DNA binding proteins facilitating condensed chromatin structure during mitosis
HMGB1: non-histone nuclear protein regulating chromatin topology during chromosome segregation
PTMA: anti-apoptotic function supporting cell survival through mitotic checkpoint
PPIA: PPIase chaperone activity stabilizing tubulin and checkpoint proteins during mitosis
suggested_validation: Live-cell imaging with STMN1 phosphorylation (CDK1-dependent inactivation) and spindle checkpoint markers (BubR1, Mad2) to confirm G2/M phase enrichment and mitotic dynamics in sorted Pre-B cells

programme_name: Megakaryocytic platelet granule biogenesis
functional_description: This feature captures megakaryocyte-specific programmes for assembly and trafficking of platelet α-granules, centred on synthesis of secretory proteins (PPBP, PF4, GP9) and their packaging into storage granules via tetraspanin-mediated membrane organisation (CD9, CMTM5). The co-expression of cytoskeletal regulators (GSN, CALD1, ILK) and lipid metabolism enzymes (ALOX12, LCN2) reflects concurrent remodelling of megakaryocyte cytoplasm during platelet production.
key_evidence: PPBP, PF4: core α-granule chemokine cargo proteins packaged into platelet storage granules
GP9: platelet membrane glycoprotein essential for GP1b-IX-V complex formation on megakaryocyte/platelet surface
CD9, CMTM5: tetraspanins and transmembrane organizers controlling granule biogenesis and membrane trafficking
GSN, CALD1: actin-binding proteins regulating cytoskeletal remodelling during megakaryocyte proplatelet extension
ALOX12, LCN2: lipid metabolism and inflammatory mediator synthesis associated with platelet activation state
suggested_validation: Perform co-immunofluorescence on megakaryocyte precursors and mature megakaryocytes using antibodies against PPBP/PF4 (α-granule cargo), CD63/CD9 (granule membrane markers), and GP9 (platelet membrane glycoprotein) to spatially validate coordinate expression during granulogenesis; correlate SAE feature activity with functional platelet granule release assays.

programme_name: Antigen presentation and immune priming
functional_description: This feature marks cells undergoing coordinated upregulation of MHC class II presentation machinery (HLA-DR, HLA-DP, HLA-DQ, CD74, HLA-DMA) alongside cytoskeletal remodeling (TMSB4X, COTL1, ANXA2) and antimicrobial effectors (LYZ). This represents the transcriptional priming of dendritic cells and megakaryocyte precursors for professional antigen-presenting function, characterized by assembly of peptide-loading compartments and morphological adaptation required for DC migration and immune synapse formation.
key_evidence: HLA-DRB1/HLA-DRA/HLA-DPA1/HLA-DPB1/HLA-DQA1/HLA-DQB1: Complete MHC class II heterodimer sets required for antigen presentation
CD74: Chaperone essential for peptide loading onto HLA class II molecules in specialized compartments
HLA-DMA: Peptide exchange catalyst specifically facilitating class II MHC loading efficiency
TMSB4X/COTL1/ANXA2: Actin-binding proteins enabling dendritic cell morphological remodeling for migration and antigen capture
LYZ: Antimicrobial effector consistent with DC microbicidal and pathogen-processing capacity
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantifying surface MHC-II (HLA-DR/DP/DQ), CD11c, and CD1c on feature-high vs feature-low cells from sorted pre-cDC and megakaryocyte precursor populations, combined with functional assay of antigen presentation capacity via OVA-peptide presentation to T cell hybridomas.

programme_name: Megakaryocyte integrin signalling and cytoskeletal assembly
functional_description: This programme coordinates megakaryocyte-specific integrin activation and cytoskeletal remodelling required for platelet production. It couples integrin signalling (ITGA2B, FERMT3, ILK, TLN1) with actin dynamics (TMSB4X, GSN, ACTN1) and platelet-specific membrane glycoproteins (GP9, SELP) essential for megakaryocyte maturation and proplatelet formation.
key_evidence: ITGA2B: αIIbβ3 integrin core adhesion receptor; megakaryocyte-restricted integrin essential for platelet function
FERMT3 (kindlin-3): integrin co-activator; directly mediates inside-out signalling required for integrin clustering and cell adhesion
TLN1 (talin): integrin cytoplasmic tail binding partner; nucleates signalling complex linking integrin to F-actin cytoskeleton
TMSB4X: actin sequestration; regulates actin polymerization dynamics critical for proplatelet morphogenesis
GSN (gelsolin): actin barbed-end capping; controls actin filament severing and depolymerization during cytoskeletal remodelling
GP9: platelet-specific tetraspan; component of GPIX complex required for GPIb-IX-V receptor function and platelet adhesion
SELP (P-selectin): α-granule membrane protein; mediates megakaryocyte-endothelial interactions and platelet adhesion
suggested_validation: Co-immunoprecipitate FERMT3 with ITGA2B and TLN1 in megakaryocyte precursors; perform TIRF microscopy to visualize integrin signalling complex assembly and actin recruitment during proplatelet formation in sorted population.

programme_name: B-cell receptor signaling and pre-B maturation
functional_description: This programme captures the transition from pro-B to small pre-B cells, marked by assembly and stabilization of the B-cell receptor complex (CD79B) coupled with checkpoint control mechanisms. The co-expression of BACH2 (a transcriptional regulator of B-cell differentiation) with DNA repair genes (NEIL1) and apoptotic regulators (HRK) reflects the critical developmental checkpoint where pre-BCR signaling is validated before further maturation.
key_evidence: CD79B: core BCR signaling component essential for pre-BCR complex formation and allelic exclusion checkpoint
BACH2: transcriptional brake on B-cell differentiation; prevents premature maturation and governs germinal center selection
NEIL1: base excision repair during V(D)J recombination and early B-cell development to manage DNA damage from RAG activity
HRK: pro-apoptotic BCL-2 family member; enforces apoptosis of cells failing pre-BCR checkpoint
FCRLA: negative regulator of BCR signaling; fine-tunes receptor-mediated activation thresholds during pre-B stage
suggested_validation: Sort Small Pre-B cells (CD19+CD10+CD79B+CD34−) and Pro-B cells (CD19+CD10+CD79B−) by flow cytometry, then perform qPCR or RNA-seq validation of BACH2, NEIL1, and HRK expression differences; alternatively, use single-cell RNA-seq to confirm co-expression patterns within BCR checkpoint transitions.

programme_name: Cytotoxic T lymphocyte effector differentiation
functional_description: This feature represents the transcriptional programme of differentiated cytotoxic T lymphocytes acquiring effector function, characterized by expression of TCR components (TRAC, TRBC1, CD8A), cytolytic granule proteins (GZMA, GZMH, PRF1, GNLY), and granule-associated factors (NKG7, CST7). The co-expression of chemokines (CCL5, IL32) alongside cytotoxic machinery indicates activated, migratory CTLs poised for target cell lysis and inflammatory cytokine release.
key_evidence: GZMA, GZMH, PRF1, GNLY: serine protease and pore-forming effectors mediating target cell apoptosis
TRAC, TRBC1, CD8A: TCR and CD8 surface molecules defining mature cytotoxic T cell identity
NKG7, CST7: granule-associated membrane and cysteine protease inhibitor proteins
CCL5, IL32: chemokines and cytokines enabling recruitment and immune activation
KLRD1, KLRB1: NK cell receptor family members indicating overlapping NK-like or memory CTL phenotype
suggested_validation: Sort bone marrow cells by CD8+CD56-/low and CD8+perforin+ populations, then perform RNA-seq or targeted qPCR to confirm coordinated upregulation of all cytolytic granule components (PRF1, GZMA, GZMH, GNLY) relative to resting T cells and proliferating progenitors.

programme_name: Proliferative metabolism and mitotic spindle assembly
functional_description: This programme coordinates active cell cycle progression through coupled glycolytic-energetic support and mitotic apparatus assembly. The feature integrates metabolic reprrogramming (PKM, ENO1, LDHA, PHGDH, GAPDH) to sustain biosynthetic and bioenergetic demands of proliferation, alongside spindle dynamics and chromatin remodeling (STMN1, TUBA1B, H2AFZ, HMGN2) required for successful mitosis. This is distinct from generic S-phase or checkpoint control, instead representing an active executioner programme in cycling Large Pre-B and megakaryocyte precursor populations.
key_evidence: STMN1: microtubule dynamics regulation—critical for spindle assembly and mitotic checkpoint control
PKM + ENO1 + GAPDH: coupled glycolytic enzyme signature supporting ATP and biosynthetic precursor generation during S/G2/M phases
TUBA1B: tubulin component essential for spindle microtubule polymerization and cytokinesis
H2AFZ + HMGN2: histone variants and chromatin architectural proteins required for condensed chromatin transition during mitosis
UBE2C: ubiquitin conjugation enzyme critical for APC/C-mediated metaphase-to-anaphase transition and mitotic progression
PHGDH + LDHA: serine synthesis and NAD+ recycling supporting nucleotide biosynthesis and redox balance in proliferating cells
suggested_validation: Time-resolved single-cell RNA-seq through synchronized cell cycle stages (e.g., nocodazole arrest-release) in sorted Large Pre-B cells, validating peak expression during G2/M phases and correlation with mitotic marker proteins (phospho-histone H3, Aurora B kinase activity).

programme_name: Ribosome biogenesis and nucleolar organization
functional_description: This programme coordinates the assembly of ribosomal subunits and nucleolar function during rapid erythroid and myeloid proliferation. The dominant ribosomal protein signatures (RPS24, RPS17, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0) reflect active 40S and 60S subunit synthesis, while HMGB1, HMGB2, and HMGN2 facilitate nucleolar chromatin accessibility and ribosomal DNA transcription. This reflects the extreme protein synthesis demands of polychromatic erythroblasts undergoing accelerated haemoglobin production.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS17, RPS23, RPL37A, RPLP0: structural components of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunits required for translation initiation and elongation
HMGB1, HMGB2: non-histone DNA-binding proteins that maintain nucleolar DNA topology and facilitate ribosomal RNA transcription
HMGN2: binds nucleosomal DNA in transcriptionally active chromatin, specifically enriched at active nucleolar regions
ANP32B: co-activator of RNA polymerase I at the nucleolus, essential for rRNA synthesis
DEK: DNA topology modulator that promotes supercoiling, facilitating high-rate rRNA transcription
suggested_validation: Quantify 45S and mature 18S/28S rRNA levels by qRT-PCR in flow-sorted polychromatic erythroblasts vs. earlier pro-erythroblasts; correlate SAE feature activation with nucleolar size by immunofluorescence against fibrillarin and UBF.

programme_name: B cell receptor signalling and lymphoid priming
functional_description: This feature captures early B lymphoid differentiation with concurrent priming for adaptive immune activation. CD79B (BCR complex component) combined with BACH2 (B cell transcription factor controlling immune response) and TOX2 (transcriptional coactivator) indicates active B cell receptor pathway engagement. The presence of DNA repair machinery (NEIL1) alongside pro-apoptotic regulators (HRK) suggests a selection checkpoint state where developing B cells undergo antigen receptor signalling and survive/apoptosis decisions.
key_evidence: CD79B: B cell antigen receptor complex essential for pre-B and immature B cell development
BACH2: Master transcriptional regulator of B cell differentiation and T cell adaptive immunity
TOX2: Transcriptional coactivator driving lymphoid gene programmes
NEIL1: DNA glycosylase active during V(D)J recombination-associated DNA damage response
HRK: BCL-2 family pro-apoptotic protein for elimination of autoreactive or non-functional B cells
suggested_validation: Sort CD79B+ pre-B cells and perform single-cell RNA-seq with TCR/BCR clonotype capture to confirm BACH2/TOX2 co-expression during productive B cell receptor signalling, and validate NEIL1 upregulation correlates with V(D)J recombination activity via quantitative PCR on RAG-mediated DNA breaks.

programme_name: Bone marrow stromal niche signalling
Aerobic glycolysis and anabolic biosynthesis burst
functional_description: Large pre-B cells activate coordinated glycolytic and biosynthetic pathways to support rapid biomass accumulation during the pre-B cell expansion phase. This programme couples elevated glycolysis (ENO1, GAPDH, LDHA) with serine/one-carbon metabolism (PHGDH) and fatty acid uptake (FABP5), providing both ATP and biosynthetic precursors. Concurrent expression of mitochondrial (VDAC1) and cytoskeletal components (ACTG1, STMN1) enables metabolic coupling with cell cycle progression and blastoid morphology.
key_evidence: ENO1, GAPDH, LDHA: glycolytic axis for ATP generation and lactate metabolism
PHGDH: serine biosynthesis gateway enabling one-carbon metabolism and nucleotide synthesis
FABP5: lipid uptake supporting membrane biogenesis during cell expansion
VDAC1: mitochondrial metabolic hub and ATP/metabolite exchange
CDCA7: c-Myc target gene coordinating proliferative metabolism
STMN1, ACTG1: microtubule and cytoskeletal remodeling during cell cycle
IGFBP7: potential growth factor signaling modulation
suggested_validation: Perform isotope tracing (13C-glucose, 13C-serine) in sorted large pre-B cells to quantify glycolytic and one-carbon flux; validate with seahorse extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) and oxygen consumption rate (OCR) measurements showing elevated aerobic glycolysis and OXPHOS coupling.

programme_name: Megakaryocyte cytoskeletal assembly and platelet biogenesis
functional_description: This programme coordinates the dramatic cytoskeletal reorganization required for megakaryocyte maturation and platelet formation. It activates actin-binding and cross-linking proteins (GSN, FLNA, ACTN1, TPM4) that establish the contractile apparatus and focal adhesions necessary for megakaryocyte proplatelet extension. Concurrent expression of platelet-specific surface markers (GP9, SELP, CD63) and integrin activation machinery (FERMT3, ZYX) prepares nascent platelets for haemostatic function.
key_evidence: GSN: nucleates and caps actin filament barbed ends critical for proplatelet cytoplasm extension
FLNA: actin-binding crosslinker essential for establishing 3D cytoskeletal architecture during proplatelet branching
GP9: platelet glycoprotein complex (GPIB-IX-V) mediating von Willebrand factor binding in haemostasis
FERMT3: kindlin-3 activates integrins (αIIbβ3) required for platelet adhesion and aggregation
ACTN1 & TPM4: spectrin-family cytoskeletal stabilizers maintaining platelet shape and deformability
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence imaging of primary human megakaryocytes to confirm coordinate localization of actin regulators (GSN, FLNA) with platelet-specific surface markers (GP9, CD63) during proplatelet stage morphogenesis

programme_name: Nuclear-cytoplasmic RNA processing in proliferation
functional_description: This programme coordinates active ribosome biogenesis and mRNA processing during rapid proliferation of lymphoid and erythroid progenitors. The dominant hnRNP proteins (A1, A2/B1, C) and NPM1 nucleophosmin regulate pre-rRNA processing and nucleolar organization, while HMGB1/HMGN factors facilitate transcriptionally active chromatin accessibility. PTMA and chaperone proteins (PPIA) support protein homeostasis during intense biosynthetic demand.
key_evidence: HNRNPA1, HNRNPA2B1, HNRNPC: RNA processing and splicing for rapid transcript generation during proliferation
NPM1: nucleolar assembly and ribosome biogenesis—rate-limiting for progenitor cell divisions
HMGB1, HMGN1, HMGN2: chromatin accessibility and transcriptional activation required for proliferative genes
SLC25A5: mitochondrial ATP/ADP exchange supporting energy-intensive biosynthesis and proliferation
PPIA: peptidyl-prolyl isomerase chaperoning nascent proteins during high-rate synthesis
suggested_validation: Quantify nucleolar size and pre-rRNA processing efficiency (qRT-PCR of 45S/47S pre-rRNA) in sorted Large Pre-B cells with NPM1 knockdown versus controls to validate nucleolar bottleneck hypothesis for this programme.

programme_name: Megakaryocytic contamination in erythroid progenitors
functional_description: This feature represents aberrant megakaryocytic gene expression within early erythroid progenitor populations, driven by platelet-lineage markers (PPBP, PF4) and megakaryocyte-specific proteins (MYL9 myosin light chain). The prevalence of these genes suggests either contamination from megakaryocyte precursors (8% of top 200 cells) or aberrant co-expression during early multipotent progenitor stages before full erythroid commitment.
key_evidence: PPBP: CXC chemokine exclusively expressed in megakaryocytes/platelets, not erythroid lineage
PF4: Alpha-granule protein marking mature megakaryocyte program, incompatible with erythroid differentiation
MYL9: Myosin regulatory light chain indicating smooth muscle/megakaryocyte cytoskeletal apparatus, absent in erythroid cells
CLEC1B: NK cell and megakaryocyte C-type lectin receptor, not erythroid-specific
suggested_validation: Sort top-200 activating cells by flow cytometry using CD34/CD38/CD41 markers to quantify megakaryocyte precursor contamination and perform RNA-seq on pure CD34+CD41− pro-erythroblasts to confirm these genes are absent in genuine early erythroid progenitors.

programme_name: Cytoskeletal remodeling in erythroid maturation
functional_description: This programme coordinates actin-binding and membrane scaffolding proteins essential for the dramatic morphological changes during erythroid differentiation, particularly the transition from polychromatic to orthochromatic erythroblasts. The co-expression of DAAM1, PARVB, DMTN, TPM1, and STOM reflects reorganization of the cortical actin cytoskeleton and stabilization of membrane architecture needed for progressive cell shrinkage, enucleation, and shape spheroidization characteristic of late erythroid maturation.
key_evidence: DMTN: actin-bundling protein essential for erythrocyte membrane stability and shape maintenance
DAAM1: formin regulating actin polymerization and cytokinesis during cell shape remodeling
PARVB: focal adhesion and cytoskeletal organization during morphological transitions
TPM1: actin-binding protein stabilizing newly remodeled cytoskeletal architecture
STOM: integral membrane protein anchoring remodeled actin structures to erythroid membrane
AHSP: chaperone ensuring proper hemoglobin assembly concurrent with cytoskeletal maturation
UROD: heme biosynthesis continuing during late-stage maturation requiring metabolic coordination
suggested_validation: Live-cell imaging of actin dynamics (phalloidin staining) and membrane deformability assays (optical stretching) in sorted polychromatic vs orthochromatic erythroblasts from DMTN/PARVB-edited vs control cultures

programme_name: MHC-II antigen presentation in myeloid progenitors
functional_description: This programme is characterized by coordinated expression of MHC class II molecules (HLA-DRA, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1) and associated chaperone machinery (CD74, HLA-DMA), indicating active antigen presentation capability. The enrichment in megakaryocyte precursors and pre-dendritic cells suggests this reflects differentiation-linked upregulation of professional APC machinery concurrent with proliferation, rather than a generic translational burst.
key_evidence: HLA-DRA/DRB1/DPA1/DPB1: Complete MHC class II heterodimer components required for peptide-MHC assembly
CD74: Chaperone essential for MHC-II loading and trafficking through endosomal compartments
HLA-DMA: Peptide exchange catalyst that optimizes MHC-II-peptide binding in specialized compartments
GSTP1/GPX1: Antioxidant enzymes supporting redox homeostasis during metabolically active differentiation
ACTG1/TMSB4X: Cytoskeletal regulators enabling dendritic cell morphodynamics and antigen uptake
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantifying HLA-DR surface expression and CD74 protein levels across the cell-type composition, combined with immunofluorescence confirming MHC-II localization to endosomal compartments in activated megakaryocyte precursors and pre-DCs.

programme_name: Megakaryocyte lineage contamination in erythroblasts
functional_description: This feature captures aberrant expression of megakaryocyte-specific genes in early erythroblasts, primarily platelet structural and secretory proteins (PPBP, PF4, MYL9) alongside myeloid pattern recognition receptors. The programme does not reflect genuine erythroid biosynthesis but rather transcriptional leakage or co-expression of megakaryocyte lineage markers in basophilic/pro-erythroblasts, likely representing either a minor contaminating population or progenitors with residual megakaryocytic priming.
key_evidence: PPBP & PF4: megakaryocyte-derived platelet proteins, not erythroid biosynthetic enzymes
MYL9: muscle/smooth muscle myosin light chain—muscle contractility marker absent in erythroid differentiation
TREML1 & CLEC1B: myeloid/NK pattern recognition receptors inconsistent with erythroid specification
LY6G6F & LCN2: innate immune proteins not involved in heme or globin biosynthesis
ILK & CALD1: cytoskeletal regulators associated with contractility, not erythroid maturation
suggested_validation: Sort basophilic erythroblasts by CD41/CD61 (megakaryocyte markers) and confirm that this feature's genes are enriched in the CD41+ fraction; perform single-cell RNA-seq to validate whether co-expression occurs within individual cells or represents population mixing.

programme_name: Ribosomal protein synthesis in erythroid progenitors
functional_description: This programme represents coordinated expression of ribosomal protein structural components (40S and 60S subunits) coupled with translation elongation factors, reflecting the intense protein synthesis demand during erythroid differentiation. The enrichment in CFU-E, Pro-Erythroblasts, and Megakaryocyte Precursors indicates activation during the proliferative phase preceding hemoglobin accumulation and terminal differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS26, RPS17, RPS23, RPS24: 40S ribosomal subunit proteins required for ribosome assembly and translational capacity
RPL37A, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL4: 60S ribosomal subunit proteins and lateral stalk components essential for peptide bond formation
EEF1B2: translation elongation factor maintaining ribosome recycling and protein chain extension efficiency
LDHB, UQCRH, SLC25A3: metabolic/mitochondrial support genes enabling ATP and amino acid availability for sustained protein synthesis
suggested_validation: Quantify ribosomal protein mRNA and protein abundance across sorted erythroid developmental stages (CFU-E → Poly-chromatic → Orthochromatic Erythroblasts) using RT-qPCR and Western blotting, correlating with polysome profiling to confirm active translational capacity in early erythroid progenitors.

programme_name: Pre-B cell receptor signalling and cycling
functional_description: This programme reflects the pre-B cell receptor (pre-BCR) complex assembly and early B cell development checkpoint. The dominant genes encode surrogate light chain components (VPREB1/3), signalling adaptors (CD79B, LAT2), and the pre-BCR ligand IGLL1, coupled with active cell cycle machinery (STMN1, MAD2L2) characteristic of pre-B cells transitioning through the large pre-B stage.
key_evidence: VPREB1/VPREB3: Core surrogate light chain components of functional pre-BCR complex
CD79B: Essential signal transduction molecule in pre-BCR signalling pathway
IGLL1: Pre-BCR ligand expressed exclusively at pro-B/pre-B stages
EBF1: Master transcription factor for B cell identity and pre-BCR checkpoint regulation
STMN1: Microtubule-destabilizing protein required for active cell cycle progression
MAD2L2: Spindle checkpoint control during proliferative phase of large pre-B cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting of pre-BCR+ (VPREB1+CD79B+IGLL1+) vs pre-BCR- B cell populations followed by bulk RNA-seq or qPCR validation of feature co-expression pattern; additionally, functional validation via pre-BCR crosslinking assays in sorted large pre-B cells to confirm active signalling pathway.

programme_name: Megakaryocyte-specific cytoskeletal and granule maturation
functional_description: This feature captures a megakaryocyte-enriched transcriptional programme focused on cytoskeletal reorganization and alpha-granule protein synthesis. The co-expression of structural proteins (MYL9, CALD1, SAMD14), platelet-specific chemokines (PPBP, PF4), coagulation factors (F13A1), and actin-binding regulators reflects the specialization of megakaryocytes for platelet generation and hemostatic function. Although basophilic and pro-erythroblasts comprise 73% of activated cells, the dominant megakaryocyte-specific gene signature suggests this feature preferentially captures the megakaryocytic differentiation branch within the mixed erythro-megakaryocyte progenitor compartment.
key_evidence: PPBP & PF4: platelet alpha-granule chemokines specific to megakaryocyte maturation and platelet activation
MYL9 & CALD1: cytoskeletal and actomyosin regulators essential for proplatelet extension morphogenesis
F13A1: coagulation factor XIII A-chain, megakaryocyte-specific hemostatic protein
SAMD14 & ILK: actin filament organization and integrin-mediated cytoskeletal anchoring in megakaryocytes
LY6G6F: megakaryocyte lineage marker expressed during platelet maturation
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence of MYL9 and PF4 in flow-sorted CD41+ megakaryocytes vs CD71+ erythroblasts to confirm megakaryocyte-specific activation, followed by RNA-FISH to validate coordinate expression of cytoskeletal and granule maturation genes in individual megakaryocytes during proplatelet formation.

programme_name: Megakaryocyte alpha-granule maturation
functional_description: This programme represents the acquisition of platelet-specific secretory granule proteins and cytoskeletal machinery in megakaryocyte precursors. The coordinated expression of alpha-granule cargo proteins (PPBP, PF4, F13A1) alongside actin-myosin regulatory factors (MYL9, CALD1, SAMD14, ILK) reflects the developmental stage when megakaryocytes undergo extensive cytoplasmic reorganisation to form platelet territories and mature their secretory apparatus.
key_evidence: PPBP: CXC chemokine platelet-derived growth factor; canonical alpha-granule cargo protein
PF4: Platelet factor 4; released from platelet alpha granules; defines megakaryocytic identity
F13A1: Coagulation factor XIII A chain; haemostatic protein sequestered in alpha granules
MYL9: Myosin light chain; essential for actin-myosin interactions during platelet biogenesis
CALD1: Caldesmon; actin and calmodulin-binding regulator critical for megakaryocyte cytoskeletal remodelling
SAMD14: Predicted actin filament binding and organisation; supports extensive cytoplasmic reorganisation
suggested_validation: Flow cytometric quantification of PPBP/PF4 co-expression with MYL9 and actin stress fibre markers (phalloidin staining) across purified megakaryocyte precursor developmental stages, or transmission electron microscopy to visualize alpha-granule accumulation and cytoplasmic reticulum organisation in feature-high cells.

programme_name: Megakaryocyte cytoskeletal maturation and integrin signalling
functional_description: This programme coordinates the assembly and organisation of the actin cytoskeleton and integrin adhesion complexes required for megakaryocyte maturation and platelet biogenesis. The gene set reflects active remodelling of the actin nucleation and crosslinking machinery (GSN, TMSB4X, ACTN1), combined with integrin-mediated signalling through kindlins and focal adhesion proteins (FERMT3, TLN1, ILK, ZYX, PDLIM1, VASP). This is consistent with the developmental stage at which megakaryocyte precursors undergo extensive cytoplasmic reorganisation and proplatelet formation.
key_evidence: GSN & TMSB4X: Actin barbed-end capping and monomer sequestration for controlled cytoskeletal assembly
FERMT3 & ILK: Integrin activation and inside-out signalling essential for megakaryocyte adhesion and spreading
TLN1, ZYX, PDLIM1, VASP: Focal adhesion and Ena-VASP complex assembly for mechanotransduction and force generation
GP9: Platelet-specific membrane glycoprotein indicating late-stage megakaryocyte differentiation
ACTN1 & TAGLN2: Actin crosslinking and smooth muscle-like contractile organisation during proplatelet extension
suggested_validation: Use immunofluorescence to visualise actin filament organisation, focal adhesion foci (TLN1, ZYX), and integrin activation (β3 conformational status) in CD41+ megakaryocyte precursors at distinct maturation stages; correlate with FERMT3/ILK phosphorylation as readout of integrin signalling intensity.

programme_name: Megakaryocytic cytoskeletal remodeling and glycolytic metabolism
functional_description: This programme coordinates cytoskeletal reorganization with heightened glycolytic flux, hallmarks of megakaryocyte precursor maturation. The co-expression of actin regulators (ACTG1, TMSB4X, STMN1) with glycolytic enzymes (PKM, LDHA, ENO1, GAPDH) reflects the dramatic morphological transformation and metabolic demands during proplatelet formation. Chromatin remodeling factors (HMGN1/2) supporting active transcription enable the massive transcriptional output required for megakaryocytic lineage commitment.
key_evidence: ACTG1, TMSB4X, STMN1: coordinate actin polymerization control—essential for megakaryocyte cytoplasmic expansion and proplatelet branching morphogenesis
PKM, LDHA, ENO1, GAPDH: glycolytic core enzymes supporting the energy demands of cytoskeletal remodeling and massive protein synthesis during megakaryopoiesis
HMGN1/2, PTMA: facilitate transcriptionally active chromatin architecture required for lineage-specific gene expression programmes in maturing megakaryocytes
VDAC1: mitochondrial outer membrane channel supporting ATP export during high-demand metabolic phase
suggested_validation: Isolate CD34+ megakaryocyte precursors at early vs. late maturation stages; use quantitative proteomics or immunofluorescence to confirm coordinated upregulation of actin regulators (ACTG1/TMSB4X) with glycolytic flux markers (lactate production assay), and correlate with proplatelet formation kinetics.
prior_programme_name: Progenitor cell proliferation and RNA processing

programme_name: Megakaryocyte cytoskeletal organization and membrane biogenesis
functional_description: This feature captures a coordinated programme of cytoskeletal assembly and membrane protein trafficking essential for megakaryocyte morphogenesis and proplatelet formation. The programme integrates actin-binding proteins (TPM1, PARVB), membrane scaffolding complexes (MPP1, BSG), and cell membrane organization (STOM) to support the dramatic cytoplasmic reorganization and membrane expansion required during megakaryocyte maturation.
key_evidence: TPM1: actin-binding protein stabilizing microfilament cytoskeleton during proplatelet extension
PARVB: parvin family member organizing actin-based cellular structures and focal adhesions
MPP1: MAGUK scaffold protein coordinating membrane protein assembly and cytoskeletal linkage
STOM: stomatin organizing membrane microdomains critical for platelet biogenesis
BSG: cell adhesion molecule regulating cell-cell interactions during megakaryocyte expansion
CAT: antioxidant defence protecting cytoskeleton from oxidative damage during intensive biosynthesis
suggested_validation: Perform immunofluorescence co-localization of TPM1, PARVB, and MPP1 with F-actin (phalloidin) and CD41 in primary megakaryocytes during proplatelet formation stages, quantifying the correlation between feature activation level and cytoskeletal organization complexity.

programme_name: Proteostasis and ribosome biogenesis in erythroid proliferation
functional_description: This programme coordinates molecular chaperone activity (Hsp70/Hsp90 family, DNAJA1, HSPE1) with ribosome assembly factors (PA2G4, NUP37) and RNA-binding proteins (HNRNPF) to manage the massive protein synthesis load during erythroid proliferation. The co-expression reflects active quality control of nascent globin chains and ribosomal proteins during the high biosynthetic demand of basophilic and pro-erythroblast stages.
key_evidence: HSPA1A/HSPA1B/HSP90AA1/HSP90AB1: Coordinated Hsp70/Hsp90 chaperone machinery essential for preventing aggregation during high-rate protein synthesis
DNAJA1/HSPE1: Hsp40 and Hsp10 co-chaperones forming functional partnership with Hsp70 for protein folding assistance
PA2G4/NUP37: Pre-ribosomal assembly and nuclear import factors supporting concurrent ribosome biogenesis during proliferation
HNRNPF/PTMA: RNA-binding proteins coordinating mRNA processing and translation licensing in rapidly dividing cells
suggested_validation: Co-immunoprecipitation or proximity labelling (BioID) in sorted basophilic erythroblasts to confirm physical interaction between Hsp70/Hsp90 chaperones and ribosomal assembly complexes; correlate with puromycin incorporation assays to link programme activity to active translation rates across erythroid maturation stages.

programme_name: Actin dynamics and cytoskeletal remodeling
functional_description: This feature captures a coordinated programme of actin-binding and cytoskeletal regulatory proteins essential for cellular motility and morphological remodeling. The enrichment of actin sequestering proteins (TMSB4X, ACTG1, TPM4), actin-binding regulatory factors (VASP, PDLIM1, AIF1), and cell adhesion molecules (PECAM1, ITGA2) indicates active cytoskeletal restructuring required for cell migration and morphogenesis. This programme is particularly prominent in megakaryocyte precursors undergoing proplatelet extension and in dendritic cell precursors establishing migratory capacity.
key_evidence: TMSB4X, ACTG1, TPM4: Direct actin nucleation and polymerization control
VASP, PDLIM1: Actin filament bundling and focal adhesion dynamics
PECAM1, ITGA2: Cell-cell and cell-matrix adhesion enabling migration
PKM, ENO1: Glycolytic energy supply sustaining cytoskeletal remodeling
AIF1, GSTP1: Calcium signaling and oxidative stress buffering during motility
suggested_validation: Live-cell imaging of phalloidin-stained actin structures in sorted megakaryocyte precursors and cDC1s expressing high vs low Feature 1471 scores, combined with quantification of protrusion dynamics and migration velocity in transwell assays.

programme_name: Cycling B-cell precursor chromatin remodeling
Megakaryocyte contamination in erythroid progenitors
functional_description: This feature reflects transcriptional spillover or genuine co-expression of megakaryocyte-specific genes (PPBP, PF4, MYL9, CALD1) within basophilic and pro-erythroblast populations, rather than a canonical erythroid differentiation programme. The enrichment of platelet factor 4, pro-platelet basic protein, and myosin light chain 9—all megakaryocyte lineage markers—suggests either physical co-clustering of megakaryocyte precursors in the sampled population or aberrant expression in early erythroid progenitors.
key_evidence: PPBP: megakaryocyte alpha-granule protein; hallmark of platelet biogenesis lineage, not erythroid
PF4: platelet chemokine released from alpha-granules; specific to megakaryocyte differentiation pathway
MYL9: myosin component essential for megakaryocyte cytoplasmic bridging and platelet release; minimal erythroid expression
CALD1: calmodulin-binding actin regulator involved in smooth muscle and megakaryocyte contractility
CLEC1B: NK and megakaryocyte receptor; not typical erythroid marker
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting of CD34+ early erythroid progenitors (CD71+GPA+) versus megakaryocyte precursors (CD41+CD42b+) followed by qRT-PCR quantification of PPBP/PF4/MYL9 expression to confirm whether these genes are genuinely co-expressed in pure erythroid populations or represent contaminating megakaryocyte cells in the original clustering.

programme_name: Erythroid heme synthesis and globin assembly
functional_description: This programme coordinates the final maturation phase of erythroid differentiation, specifically coupling heme biosynthesis (ALAS2, HMBS, FECH) with hemoglobin assembly and stabilization (HBB, AHSP). The convergence of mitochondrial iron import (SLC25A37), heme synthesis enzymes, and globin chaperone machinery reflects the critical haem-globin stoichiometry checkpoint that guards against toxic free globin precipitation in late polychromatic erythroblasts.
key_evidence: ALAS2: erythroid-specific first committed step of heme biosynthesis—rate-limiting for Hb production
FECH: terminal heme synthesis enzyme catalysing iron insertion into protoporphyrin IX
HBB: structural globin chain; must be coordinated with haem availability to prevent aggregation
AHSP: molecular chaperone specific for free alpha-globin, preventing precipitation before β-globin pairing
SLC25A37: mitochondrial iron importer essential for haem iron supply—functional bottleneck for Hb synthesis
HMBS: committed intermediate step in heme biosynthetic pathway
suggested_validation: Quantify haem:globin ratio by HPLC and spectrophotometry in sorted polychromatic erythroblasts, measuring ALAS2/FECH protein levels in parallel. CRISPR knockout of AHSP or SLC25A37 should trigger globin precipitation and apoptosis specifically in this developmental window, validating the checkpoint function.

programme_name: Megakaryocyte granule and integrin maturation
functional_description: This programme coordinates assembly of platelet-specific organelles and adhesion complexes required for megakaryocyte terminal differentiation. It encompasses α-granule protein packaging (SELP, PF4, MMRN1, PROS1), integrin activation scaffolding (FERMT3, ITGA2B, PDLIM1), and cytoskeletal reorganization (TMSB4X, GSN, ACTN1) necessary for proplatelet formation and platelet release.
key_evidence: FERMT3: Kindlin-3 mediates integrin αIIbβ3 activation—essential for platelet adhesion and aggregation
ITGA2B: Encodes integrin αIIb subunit; forms heterodimer with β3 for platelet function
SELP: P-selectin stored in α-granules; released upon activation for platelet-cell interactions
PF4: CXC chemokine packaged in α-granules; hemostatic and immunomodulatory roles
FERMT3 + PDLIM1 + ACTN1: Coordinated integrin signalling and cytoskeletal linkage for mechanotransduction
GSN + TMSB4X: Actin dynamics regulating megakaryocyte morphology and proplatelet extension
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry quantifying surface integrin αIIbβ3 and P-selectin expression, combined with confocal microscopy of α-granule accumulation (PF4, SELP) and actin filament organization during ex vivo megakaryocyte differentiation in cells with FERMT3 or ITGA2B knockdown

programme_name: Megakaryocyte α-granule biogenesis and assembly
functional_description: This programme drives the synthesis and packaging of platelet α-granule contents in megakaryocyte precursors. The coordinated expression of secreted chemokines (PPBP, PF4), platelet surface glycoproteins (GP1BA, GP9), and membrane trafficking regulators (CMTM5, ILK) reflects the specialised biosynthetic activity required for megakaryocyte maturation and platelet biogenesis. The presence of erythroid cells likely reflects transient co-expression during the early bipotent MEP stage before lineage commitment.
key_evidence: PPBP: Canonical α-granule cargo protein and CXC chemokine released from activated platelets
PF4: Major α-granule chemokine with anticoagulant and immune regulatory functions
GP1BA & GP9: Essential platelet adhesion receptors assembled during α-granule biogenesis
CMTM5: Multi-pass membrane protein supporting intracellular trafficking to specialized granules
ILK: Integrin signalling mediator linking extracellular matrix interactions to granule dynamics
suggested_validation: Sort CD34+ megakaryocyte precursors by developmental stage (CFU-Mk assay) and perform qPCR validation of α-granule cargo genes (PPBP, PF4) and traffickers (CMTM5, ILK) across progenitor vs. mature megakaryocytes to confirm stage-specific upregulation of granule biogenesis machinery.

programme_name: Integrin-mediated cytoskeletal organization in megakaryocytes
functional_description: This programme coordinates actin cytoskeleton remodeling and integrin signaling required for megakaryocyte maturation and platelet biogenesis. The feature is driven primarily by megakaryocyte precursors (51%) and enriched for focal adhesion proteins (talin, kindlin, parvins) that stabilize integrin complexes, coupled with actin-binding and actin-nucleating factors (tropomyosin, thymosin, DAAM1) essential for proplatelet formation and membrane reorganization.
key_evidence: GP9: platelet-specific glycoprotein IX, direct marker of megakaryocyte differentiation
FERMT3: kindlin-3 mediates integrin activation critical for megakaryocyte adhesion and platelet function
TLN1: talin scaffolds integrin signaling complexes at focal adhesions during megakaryocyte maturation
DAAM1: actin nucleator essential for cytoskeletal reorganization during proplatelet extension
TTK: checkpoint kinase regulating megakaryocyte endomitosis and polyploidy
TPM1/TMSB4X: actin regulators controlling cytoskeletal dynamics during megakaryocyte morphogenesis
suggested_validation: Co-immunofluorescence of GP9 with talin and kindlin-3 in sorted megakaryocytes, followed by integrin activation assays (using JON/A antibody) to confirm functional integrin signaling during proplatelet formation stages

programme_name: DNA replication coupled heme biosynthesis
functional_description: A coordinated programme active in early-to-mid stage erythroid progenitors that synchronises S-phase DNA replication machinery (PCNA, MCM7, RPA3, DUT, TFDP1) with heme biosynthesis (UROD, BLVRB). This reflects the developmental requirement for simultaneous nuclear proliferation and cytoplasmic haem accumulation before haemoglobin synthesis in basophilic and polychromatic erythroblasts. Oxidative stress management (PRDX2, SOD1) supports the energetically demanding dual biosynthetic processes.
key_evidence: PCNA, MCM7, RPA3, DUT, TFDP1: core S-phase replication licensing and nucleotide synthesis—essential for erythroid progenitor cell cycle progression
UROD, BLVRB: sequential heme biosynthetic pathway enzymes—required for haem availability coinciding with proliferative expansion
PRDX2, SOD1: antioxidant defences—necessary to manage ROS from concurrent DNA replication and haem biosynthesis in metabolically active progenitors
suggested_validation: Isolate basophilic and polychromatic erythroblasts by flow cytometry, perform dual pulse-chase labelling with BrdU (DNA synthesis) and δ-ALA (heme biosynthesis intermediate), then quantify co-labelling frequency to confirm synchronised replication-haem biosynthesis coupling. Validate by UROD/BLVRB knockdown effects on erythroid colony formation kinetics.

programme_name: Progenitor proliferation and cell cycle licensing
functional_description: This programme coordinates G1/S cell cycle progression and proliferative licensing in early erythroid progenitors through CDK6-dependent checkpoint control and MYC-driven biosynthetic expansion. The co-expression of MYB (master regulator of erythroid lineage specification), CDK6 (G1/S kinase), MYC (proliferation driver), and HSP90AB1 (checkpoint protein chaperone) indicates active preparation for terminal erythroid differentiation while maintaining proliferative capacity in Pro-Erythroblasts and CFU-E.
key_evidence: CDK6: G1/S cyclin-dependent kinase essential for cell cycle entry and proliferative licensing in progenitors
MYC: Proto-oncogene driving anabolic programmes and cell cycle progression; required for erythroid progenitor expansion
MYB: Master transcriptional regulator of erythroid lineage commitment and proliferation control
HSP90AB1: Heat shock protein chaperoning checkpoint kinases and signalling proteins during cell cycle transitions
LYAR: DNA-binding factor implicated in transcriptional regulation during proliferative states
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry sorting of Pro-Erythroblasts and CFU-E by Ki-67/DAPI to isolate G1-phase cells, then measure CDK6 kinase activity and phospho-Rb levels; correlate feature activity with BrdU incorporation kinetics across erythroid differentiation stages.
